functional_description: This feature identifies early-stage erythroblasts undergoing active mitochondrial expansion and oxidative metabolism establishment. key_evidence: P4HB + PDIA6 + CALR: ER protein folding capacity essential for early erythropoiesis when cells synthesize large volumes of globin chains

PRDX4 + HSPB1: Oxidative stress management accompanying elevated mitochondrial respiration and iron processing in early erythroid cells
suggested_validation: Sort top-200 activating cells by CD71/CD235a (transferrin receptor/glycophorin A) and verify NDUFC1/MRPL20 expression peaks in CD71hi CD235a+ early erythroblasts; perform Seahorse mitochondrial stress test on FACS-isolated pro/basophilic vs polychromatic erythroblasts to confirm elevated basal respiration in feature-high cells.

P4HB: Prolyl hydroxylase with dual roles in collagen-like Ig domain stabilization and disulfide bond formation
PDIA6: ER-resident protein disulfide isomerase directly involved in Ig chain assembly
HSP90B1: ER-resident Hsp90 variant critical for client protein folding during high secretory demand
RPS26/RPS24/RPS17/RPS23/RPL37A/RPLP0: Coordinated ribosomal protein upregulation reflecting increased translation capacity for Ig synthesis
HSPB1: Cytosolic HSP20 stress responder supporting ER proteostasis during secretory burden
suggested_validation: Perform single-cell metabolic labeling (SunTag or puromycin assay) combined with immunofluorescence to directly quantify translational activity and ER stress (BiP/GRP78 activation) in NUCB2/CALR co-expressing cells versus bulk plasma cells

PRDX4, HSPB1: Mitochondrial and ER-localised antioxidant proteins protecting against ROS generated by intense OXPHOS during haemoglobin synthesis
UQCRQ, ATP5MF, ATP5IF1, NDUFC1: Core OXPHOS machinery components indicating metabolic transition from glycolysis to oxidative phosphorylation in pro- to basophilic erythroblasts

ACADVL: Fatty acid β-oxidation enzyme supporting mitochondrial fuel diversification in energy-demanding early erythroblasts

prior_zero_shot_name: ER stress and secretory protein processing
programme_name: ER protein synthesis and secretory pathway maturation
functional_description: This programme represents the transcriptional signature of cells with elevated secretory capacity, combining ER translocon components (SSR4, SEC11C), protein disulfide isomerases (PDIA4, PDIA6, P4HB), and ER chaperones (SDF2L1, LMAN1). SDF2L1: ER chaperone cofactor mediating refolding of misfolded secretory proteins—diagnostic of ER stress response in high-secretion cells
LMAN1: ERGIC lectin involved in ER-Golgi trafficking and retention of misfolded proteins—marks active secretory traffic
SEC11C: Signal peptidase subunit for N-terminal signal sequence cleavage—required for co-translational translocation
suggested_validation: Co-stain plasma cells and basophilic erythroblasts with XBP1s immunofluorescence (UPR activation) and ER-tracker dyes, then perform SAE feature activation analysis; correlate feature scores with intracellular immunoglobulin content (flow cytometry) and haemoglobin synthesis rates (pulsed O-propargyl-puromycin labelling)

prior_zero_shot_name: ER protein folding and secretory pathway
programme_name: Plasma cell secretory pathway maturation

SSR4, LMAN1: translocon-associated and ER-resident trafficking machinery diagnostic of active secretory pathway

MT-CO2/3, MT-ND5: mitochondrial OXPHOS genes reflecting energetic demand for sustained protein synthesis
CD63: tetraspanin involved in vesicular trafficking and membrane compartmentalization during secretion

prior_zero_shot_name: ER protein folding and secretory load
programme_name: ER proteostasis in early erythroid differentiation
functional_description: This feature captures activation of the endoplasmic reticulum protein folding and quality control machinery in early-stage erythroid cells (pro-erythroblasts and basophilic erythroblasts). key_evidence: CALR: Canonical ER chaperone essential for proper folding of haemoglobin and early secretory pathway proteins during erythroid differentiation
HSP90B1: ER-resident heat shock protein critical for maintaining proteostasis under high protein synthesis load of early erythropoiesis
P4HB & PDIA6: ER protein disulfide isomerases required for forming correct disulfide bonds in nascent globin chains and membrane proteins
SSR4: Translocon-associated protein complex subunit directly involved in translating and translocating nascent secretory/membrane proteins
DAD1 & CD59: Anti-apoptotic mechanisms protecting erythroid precursors from ER stress-induced cell death during intensive protein synthesis

prior_zero_shot_name: Mitochondrial OXPHOS and ER protein processing

functional_description: Early-stage erythroblasts (pro- and basophilic) activate a coordinated programme of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and endoplasmic reticulum protein processing to support rapid haemoglobin synthesis and erythroid maturation. key_evidence: UQCRQ, ATP5MF, ATP5MC3: Complex III and ATP synthase subunits diagnostic of high OXPHOS demand in proliferating early erythroblasts
P4HB, PDIA6, CANX: ER oxidoreductases and chaperones essential for haemoglobin quaternary structure assembly
ACADVL: Fatty acid β-oxidation for ATP generation supporting biosynthetic demand of early erythroid proliferation
SRM: Polyamine synthesis for rapid DNA replication and cell division in pro- and basophilic erythroblasts
MRPL51/52: Mitochondrial ribosomal proteins reflecting concurrent mitochondrial protein synthesis alongside nuclear-encoded globins
suggested_validation: Perform oxygen consumption rate (OCR) and extracellular acidification rate (ECAR) assays on FACS-sorted pro-erythroblasts vs basophilic erythroblasts to quantify mitochondrial ATP synthetic capacity and correlate with SAE feature activation scores across the developmental trajectory.

programme_name: IgLambda light chain ER quality control
functional_description: This programme represents specialised plasma cells actively secreting lambda light chain-containing immunoglobulins, characterised by coordinated expression of signal peptide processing (SEC11C, SSR4), ER protein quality control machinery (PDIA6, FKBP11, FKBP2, P4HB), and redox homeostasis (PRDX4). XBP1 activation drives the unfolded protein response to support high-capacity immunoglobulin synthesis and secretion.
key_evidence: IGLC2: Diagnostic lambda light chain constant region; 100% plasma cell specificity indicates mature secretory compartment
XBP1: Master regulator of ER-stress response in plasma cells; drives ER chaperone induction and ERAD capacity
PDIA6, P4HB, FKBP11, FKBP2: ER protein disulfide isomerases essential for Ig heavy-light chain pairing and disulfide bond formation
SEC11C, SSR4: Signal peptide processing complex required for translocation of secretory Ig into ER lumen
PRDX4: ER-localised antioxidant protecting misfolded Ig intermediates during oxidative folding of disulfide bonds
suggested_validation: Sort IGLC2+ plasma cells and perform immunofluorescence co-staining of PDIA6 and FKBP11 with IgLambda and IgKappa to confirm lambda-restricted ER quality control programme segregation from kappa-producing cells.

programme_name: IgKappa light chain ER folding quality control
functional_description: This programme coordinates ER-resident protein folding machinery specifically engaged during kappa light chain synthesis and secretion in plasma cells. The signature reflects active disulfide isomerization (PDIA6, P4HB), prolyl isomerization (FKBP11, FKBP2), signal peptide processing (SEC11C), and N-glycan recognition (ERLEC1) coupled to oxidative stress management (PRDX4) within the ER lumen. XBP1 transcriptional activation of ER chaperones and the presence of cargo-handling proteins (MZB1, ITM2C, CD63) indicate coordinated engagement of the unfolded protein response specifically supporting high-volume immunoglobulin kappa secretion.
key_evidence: IGKC: Defines the kappa light chain as the primary protein cargo driving ER load in this plasma cell subset
PDIA6, P4HB, FKBP11, FKBP2: Diagnostic complement of disulfide isomerases and prolyl isomerases required for kappa light chain disulfide bond maturation—not generically all plasma cells
XBP1: UPR-driven ER chaperone transcription factor, specifically activated by kappa secretion burden
SEC11C, ERLEC1: Signal peptide removal and N-glycan quality control gatekeepers for nascent kappa chain entry and glycoprotein folding checkpoints
PRDX4: ER-resident antioxidant protecting disulfide bond formation during high-throughput kappa folding
MZB1, CD63, ITM2C: ER-to-secretory pathway organelle markers indicating sustained secretory flux
suggested_validation: Co-immunoprecipitate PDIA6 with IGKC nascent chains in kappa+ plasma cells; validate XBP1-dependent induction of FKBP11/FKBP2 is specifically enriched in kappa+ vs lambda+ plasma cells by RT-qPCR and ChIP-seq at the XBP1 binding motifs in these gene promoters.

programme_name: XBP1-driven ER chaperone and ERAD coordination
functional_description: This programme orchestrates the unfolded protein response (UPR) in plasma cells through XBP1-mediated transcriptional control of ER chaperones (FKBP11, FKBP2, PRDX4), signal peptide processing machinery (SSR4, SEC11C), and ER-associated degradation (ERAD) components (DERL3, ERLEC1). The coordinated upregulation of peptidyl-prolyl isomerases and oxidative stress management enzymes supports massive immunoglobulin light chain (IGLC3) folding and quality control, with DERL3 and ERLEC1 enabling retrotranslocation of misfolded proteins for proteasomal clearance.
key_evidence: XBP1: master transcription factor driving plasma cell-specific ER expansion and UPR target gene activation
SSR4: translocon component essential for co-translational translocation of nascent immunoglobulin heavy and light chains
FKBP11, FKBP2: peptidyl-prolyl isomerases catalysing proline-rich immunoglobulin domain folding
SEC11C: signal peptidase required for N-terminal signal peptide removal from secreted Ig molecules
DERL3: derlin family ERAD component mediating retrotranslocation of misfolded Ig from ER lumen
ERLEC1: ER lectins recognising N-glycans on misfolded proteins for ERAD targeting
IGLC3: immunoglobulin lambda light chain—the substrate being quality-controlled by this pathway
PRDX4: ER-localised peroxiredoxin managing oxidative stress from disulphide bond formation in Ig domains
suggested_validation: Co-immunofluorescence of XBP1s (spliced form) with DERL3 and FKBP11 in isolated bone marrow plasma cells, combined with XBP1 ChIP-seq to confirm direct transcriptional regulation of FKBP11, SEC11C and DERL3 in primary plasma cells vs non-secretory B cells

programme_name: IgKappa light chain ER quality control and ERAD
functional_description: This programme coordinates IgKappa light chain secretion through integrated ER proteostasis mechanisms: signal peptide processing (SEC11C), proline isomerization for proper folding (FKBP11, FKBP2), disulfide bond formation (PDIA6), N-glycan recognition and ERAD substrate selection (ERLEC1), and oxidative stress management (PRDX4). XBP1 transcriptional control and translocon components (SSR4) ensure coordinated ER translocation and quality control of IgKappa molecules, while anti-apoptotic signalling (DAD1) and ER-resident chaperone support (MZB1) maintain plasma cell viability during high-load protein secretion.

XBP1: IRE1α-independent transcription factor; master regulator of ER expansion and UPR-responsive chaperone induction in secretory cells
PDIA6: Protein disulfide isomerase essential for disulfide bond formation in immunoglobulin heavy-light chain pairing
ERLEC1: ER lectin mediating N-glycan-dependent ERAD recognition; quality control gatekeeper for misfolded Ig
SEC11C: Signal peptidase catalysing N-terminal signal sequence cleavage during ER translocation of IgKappa
FKBP11: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerase essential for proline-rich Ig folding kinetics; rate-limiting folding catalyst
PRDX4: ER-localised antioxidant controlling oxidative folding environment for disulfide bond formation
DAD1: Anti-apoptotic protein enabling plasma cell survival under ER proteostatic stress
suggested_validation: Perform single-cell proteomics (e.g., CITE-seq) combining surface IgKappa detection with intracellular XBP1-GFP reporter and PDIA6/ERLEC1 abundance quantification across plasma cell maturation stages; validate with selective ERLEC1 inhibition to demonstrate ERAD-dependent IgKappa quality control.

programme_name: ER protein folding and disulfide bond maturation
functional_description: This programme reflects the acute ER proteostasis demands of antibody-secreting plasma cells, specifically coordinating protein disulfide isomerase (PDI) family members (PDIA6, P4HB), peptidyl-prolyl isomerases (FKBP11, FKBP2), and translocon machinery (SSR4, SEC11C) to facilitate immunoglobulin heavy and light chain folding. The co-expression of XBP1 (IRE1α-cleaved UPR master regulator), ER oxidoreductases (PRDX4), and ER-resident chaperone co-factors (MZB1, DAD1) indicates active XBP1s-driven transcription of the ER folding machinery programme rather than PERK-mediated translational shutdown, consistent with sustained antibody synthesis.
key_evidence: PDIA6, P4HB, FKBP11, FKBP2: core disulfide isomerase and peptidyl-prolyl isomerase enzymes required for proper Ig domain folding and inter-chain disulfide bond formation
SSR4, SEC11C: translocon-associated complex enabling co-translational translocation and N-terminal signal peptide processing of secretory Ig

PRDX4: ER-localized antioxidant peroxiredoxin maintaining redox environment for oxidative protein folding

programme_name: IgKappa light chain ER quality control

It combines signal peptide processing (SEC11C, SSR4), disulfide bond isomerization and chaperone-assisted folding (PDIA6, P4HB, FKBP11), and ER-resident quality control machinery (ERLEC1 for N-glycan recognition, ITM2C for ERAD regulation). XBP1: Master UPR transcription factor essential for plasma cell ER expansion and chaperone induction
PDIA6, P4HB, FKBP11: ER protein disulfide isomerases and prolyl isomerases required for Ig heavy-light chain pairing and quaternary structure
SEC11C, SSR4: Signal peptide processing complex essential for translocation of nascent Ig chains across ER membrane
ERLEC1: N-glycan-dependent ER quality control lectin; gates ERAD of misfolded Ig
DAD1: Core OST subunit supporting N-glycosylation during Ig synthesis; anti-apoptotic signal for ER stress survival

programme_name: IgKappa light chain ER translocation quality control
functional_description: This programme represents the early secretory pathway commitment in kappa light chain-secreting plasma cells, characterised by coordinated upregulation of signal peptidase complex components (SEC11C, SSR4), prolyl isomerases (FKBP11, FKBP2), and disulfide isomerase machinery (PDIA6, P4HB) that facilitate cotranslational translocation and initial folding of IGKC transcripts. SEC11C: Signal peptidase component essential for co-translational cleavage of IGKC signal peptide during translocon-mediated translocation
SSR4: Translocon-associated protein complex delta subunit, directly facilitates nascent polypeptide insertion into ER lumen during synthesis
FKBP11/FKBP2: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerases catalysing proline cis-trans isomerisation critical for efficient light chain folding kinetics

programme_name: IgLambda light chain ER folding quality control
functional_description: This programme represents the endoplasmic reticulum protein folding and quality control machinery specifically engaged during lambda light chain immunoglobulin synthesis in plasma cells. The coordinated expression of peptidyl-prolyl isomerases (FKBP11, FKBP2), protein disulfide isomerases (PDIA6, P4HB), and the signal peptidase SEC11C reflects active co-translational translocation and disulfide bond formation required for Ig lambda chain assembly. programme_name: IgKappa ER quality control and ERAD initiation
functional_description: This programme coordinates the early stages of IgKappa light chain secretion through ER translocation, N-glycan recognition-mediated quality control, and initiation of ER-associated degradation (ERAD) pathways. The co-expression of signal peptidase (SEC11C), translocon machinery (SSR4), peptidyl-prolyl isomerase (FKBP11), and ERAD-initiating lectins (ERLEC1) indicates active surveillance of newly synthesized IgKappa for proper folding, with defective molecules routed to proteasomal degradation via HERPUD1-mediated ubiquitination.

FKBP11: Prolyl isomerase accelerating proline cis/trans isomerization—rate-limiting step in Ig heavy chain pairing and light chain folding

PDIA6: PDI family disulfide isomerase catalyzing inter-chain and intra-chain disulfide bond formation essential for Ig stability

suggested_validation: Perform co-immunoprecipitation of ERLEC1 with IGKC and HERPUD1 in IgKappa+ plasma cells, combined with pulse-chase labeling and proteasome inhibition to directly quantify ERAD flux of misfolded kappa chains.

programme_name: IgLambda light chain ER quality control
functional_description: This programme mediates secretion-competent IgLambda light chain folding and quality control in plasma cells. It couples translocon-mediated translocation (SSR4, SEC11C) with prolyl isomerase-driven proline-rich domain folding (FKBP11, FKBP2) and ER chaperone-assisted refolding (SDF2L1, MZB1), while preventing accumulation of misfolded protein through antioxidant buffering (PRDX4) and selective autophagy (CD63, DAD1). XBP1-driven transcriptional coordination ensures co-expression of this integrated ER proteostasis network under high secretory demand.

SSR4: Signal sequence recognition particle component essential for co-translational translocation of all Ig chains
FKBP11: Prolyl isomerase specifically required for proline-rich Ig domain folding kinetics
SEC11C: Signal peptidase catalysing removal of lambda light chain signal peptide post-translocation
SDF2L1: ER-resident chaperone cofactor binding misfolded Ig domains for refolding or triage
PRDX4: ER-luminal redox buffer preventing disulphide bond mispairing in multi-domain lambda chain
XBP1: Master IRE1α-dependent transcription factor driving plasma cell ER chaperone programme
MZB1: Plasma cell-enriched ER-to-Golgi cargo adaptor stabilising secretory pathway fidelity
DAD1: BAX inhibitor within translocon preventing ERAD-independent apoptosis during ER stress
CD63: Tetraspanin marking CUPS/lysosomes mediating selective autophagy of terminally misfolded Ig
suggested_validation: Perform XBP1-driven ChIP-seq in primary bone marrow plasma cells to validate direct transcriptional control of SEC11C, FKBP11, SDF2L1, and SSR4; validate by treating with IRE1α RNase inhibitor (STF-083010) and measuring IgLambda secretion capacity and ER chaperone downregulation by qRT-PCR and FACS.

programme_name: IgLambda light chain ER translocation and disulfide folding
functional_description: This programme orchestrates co-translational translocation and oxidative folding of immunoglobulin lambda light chains during plasma cell differentiation. The feature captures the coordinated induction of translocon machinery (SSR4, SEC11C), ER-resident protein disulfide isomerases (PDIA6, P4HB, FKBP11), and redox homeostasis enzymes (PRDX4) required for efficient lambda Ig assembly. MZB1 and MYDGF provide additional ER-resident survival signals during the IgLambda-secreting phase.
key_evidence: IGLC2: diagnostic marker of lambda light chain expression; directly demonstrates IgLambda-restricted differentiation state
SSR4: delta subunit of Sec61 translocon complex—essential for co-translational translocation of nascent Ig chains
SEC11C: signal peptidase catalyzes cleavage of Ig signal peptides during translocation; rate-limiting for chain processing
PDIA6 & P4HB: protein disulfide isomerases catalyze oxidative folding of conserved lambda disulfide bonds (Cys23-Cys92)
FKBP11 & FKBP2: prolyl isomerases accelerate proline-containing domain folding in lambda variable regions

programme_name: IgKappa ER translocation and disulfide isomerase folding
functional_description: This programme coordinates co-translational translocation of IgKappa light chains through the ER translocon (SSR4, SEC11C) with oxidative protein folding via disulfide isomerases (PDIA6, P4HB) and peptidyl-prolyl isomerases (FKBP11, FKBP2). XBP1-mediated transcriptional induction sustains the ER chaperone machinery during high-flux immunoglobulin secretion, supported by ER-resident quality control factors (PRDX4 for redox homeostasis, DAD1 for apoptosis protection during proteotoxic stress).
key_evidence: IGKC: IgKappa constant domain—sole immunoglobulin isotype in this feature; diagnostic of kappa-restricted plasma cells
SSR4: Translocon-associated protein delta subunit—essential for signal peptide-dependent ER translocation of nascent Ig
PDIA6: Protein disulfide isomerase family member—catalyses inter-chain and intra-chain disulfide bond formation critical for Ig assembly
XBP1: UPR-activated transcription factor—master regulator of ER chaperone expression during plasma cell differentiation
SEC11C: Signal peptidase catalytic subunit—cleaves signal peptides post-translocation; rate-limiting for secretory pathway

P4HB: Prolyl 4-hydroxylase beta (PDI)—multifunctional ER chaperone with isomerase and oxidoreductase activity
suggested_validation: Co-immunoprecipitate XBP1s-bound chromatin from IgKappa+ plasma cells using ChIP-seq, validating enrichment at PDIA6, P4HB, SSR4, and SEC11C promoters; correlate XBP1 binding intensity with ER chaperone mRNA expression in single-cell RNA-seq stratified by kappa/lambda status.

programme_name: IgKappa light chain ER translocation and disulfide isomerization
functional_description: This programme orchestrates co-translational translocation and post-translational quality control of IgKappa light chains through the translocon (SSR4, SEC11C) and ER lumen oxidoreductases (PDIA6, P4HB, FKBP11). The presence of IGKC, XBP1, and DAD1 indicates active kappa light chain synthesis with integrated ER stress sensing and anti-apoptotic survival signalling to tolerate the high secretory protein burden.

SSR4: translocon-associated protein delta subunit essential for co-translational translocation of kappa chains into ER lumen
PDIA6: protein disulfide isomerase catalysing disulfide bond formation critical for kappa light chain folding stability
P4HB: prolyl 4-hydroxylase providing proline hydroxylation necessary for kappa chain structural integrity
FKBP11: peptidyl-prolyl isomerase accelerating kappa chain proline residue isomerization during folding
XBP1: UPR transcription factor upregulated to sustain ER chaperone and translocon capacity for kappa chain synthesis
DAD1: anti-apoptotic defender protecting plasma cells from ER stress-induced death during high-rate kappa secretion
suggested_validation: Co-immunoprecipitation of IGKC with SSR4 and PDIA6 in sorted IgKappa+ plasma cells to confirm functional translocon-oxidoreductase complex assembly during kappa chain translocation and folding

programme_name: IgKappa ER translocation and peptidyl-prolyl isomerase folding
functional_description: This programme coordinates co-translational translocation of IgKappa light chains via the SSR4-containing translocon complex, with concurrent assistance from peptidyl-prolyl cis/trans isomerases (FKBP11, FKBP2) and disulfide isomerases (PDIA6, P4HB) to facilitate proper folding of immunoglobulin in the ER lumen. XBP1 activation supports the transcriptional coordination of this secretory capacity, while PRDX4 provides antioxidant protection against oxidative stress during high-rate Ig synthesis.
key_evidence: IGKC: diagnostic IgKappa light chain constant region—defines kappa-restricted plasma cells
SSR4: translocon-associated protein delta subunit essential for co-translational translocation of signal peptide-containing nascent Ig chains
FKBP11: peptidyl-prolyl isomerase accelerating folding of proline-rich Ig domains
FKBP2: immunophilin family PPIase supporting Ig chain folding kinetics
PDIA6: protein disulfide isomerase catalysing disulfide bond formation critical for Ig tertiary structure
P4HB: prolyl 4-hydroxylase providing post-translational collagen-like modifications and disulfide isomerase activity
XBP1: UPR-regulated transcription factor controlling ER chaperone and translocon expression in plasma cells
PRDX4: ER-localised peroxiredoxin protecting against oxidative stress during intensive protein synthesis
SEC11C: signal peptidase cleavage of nascent Ig signal peptides during translocation
DAD1: OST48 component protecting against ER stress-induced apoptosis during Ig secretion
suggested_validation: Surface IgKappa+ intracellular flow cytometry combined with selective PDIA6 or FKBP11 inhibition to demonstrate quantitative reduction in intracellular IgKappa folding and secretion rate in purified plasma cells

programme_name: IgKappa light chain ER quality control
functional_description: This feature captures the unfolded protein response (UPR) and ER quality control machinery specifically activated during IgKappa light chain synthesis and secretion in plasma cells. The programme combines signal peptide processing (SEC11C), prolyl isomerase-catalysed folding (FKBP11, P4HB, PDIA6), N-glycan ER-associated degradation (ERLEC1), and oxidative protein folding protection (PRDX4), coordinated by XBP1-driven transcriptional regulation of ER chaperones.
key_evidence: IGKC: diagnostic IgKappa light chain transcript; exclusive to kappa-expressing plasma cells
XBP1: master transcription factor for UPR initiation and ER chaperone induction in secretory plasma cells
SEC11C: signal peptidase mediating co-translational translocation of Ig heavy/light chains into ER lumen
FKBP11: peptidyl-prolyl isomerase essential for correct disulfide bond formation in immunoglobulin framework regions
P4HB: protein disulfide isomerase catalysing oxidative folding of Ig constant domains; highly abundant in secretory cells
PDIA6: ER-resident disulfide isomerase facilitating Ig heavy-light chain pairing and stability
ERLEC1: N-glycan-dependent ER quality control lectin preventing secretion of misfolded Ig
PRDX4: ER-resident antioxidant protecting nascent Ig from oxidative damage during folding
DAD1: subunit of oligosaccharyltransferase complex ensuring N-glycosylation fidelity on Ig constant regions
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry sort IgKappa+ vs IgLambda+ plasma cells, perform RT-qPCR validation of XBP1 splicing status and FKBP11/PDIA6/ERLEC1 expression ratios; compare to IgLambda-restricted feature to confirm kappa-specificity of this ER quality control signature

programme_name: IgKappa light chain ER translocation and disulfide maturation
functional_description: This programme defines kappa light chain-secreting plasma cells executing co-translational translocation via the SEC61 translocon (SSR4, SEC11C) coupled to oxidative protein folding in the ER lumen. The coordinated expression of protein disulfide isomerases (PDIA6, P4HB), peptidyl-prolyl isomerases (FKBP11), and the ER-resident chaperone machinery (XBP1-regulated transcripts) ensures proper maturation of disulfide bonds in immunoglobulin kappa chains before secretion. PRDX4 and DAD1 provide redox homeostasis and anti-apoptotic signalling to survive the ER stress of high-rate immunoglobulin synthesis.
key_evidence: IGKC: diagnostic marker of kappa light chain-secreting plasma cells; sole immunoglobulin light chain gene in top 15
SSR4: delta subunit of translocon-associated protein; essential for co-translational translocation of IGKC signal peptide into ER lumen
PDIA6, P4HB: protein disulfide isomerases catalysing disulfide bond formation critical for Ig kappa tertiary structure and stability
FKBP11: peptidyl-prolyl isomerase facilitating proline-rich kappa constant region folding
XBP1: master regulator of ER chaperone induction during UPR; transcription factor driving expression of folding machinery
SEC11C: signal peptidase component cleaving IGKC signal sequence post-translocation
PRDX4: ER-localised peroxiredoxin maintaining redox balance during oxidative protein folding
DAD1: anti-apoptotic OST3/DAD1 subunit of oligosaccharyltransferase; prevents ER stress-induced death
suggested_validation: Perform ER fractionation on FACS-sorted IGKC+/IGLC- plasma cells, quantify disulfide bond maturation by non-reducing vs reducing SDS-PAGE, and measure XBP1s splicing kinetics during the secretory burst using qRT-PCR.

programme_name: IgG heavy chain ER translocation and proline isomerization
functional_description: This programme coordinates co-translational translocation of IgG heavy chains (IGHG1/IGHG3) through the translocon complex and subsequent ER lumenal proline isomerization. SSR4 and SEC11C mediate signal peptide recognition and cleavage during translocation, while FKBP11 (peptidyl-prolyl isomerase) facilitates proper folding of proline-rich immunoglobulin domains essential for quaternary structure. Co-expression of IGKC indicates concurrent light chain synthesis optimised for heavy-light chain pairing.
key_evidence: IGHG3, IGHG1: Heavy chain transcripts diagnostic of IgG-secreting plasma cells; IGHG3 typically higher in cytokine-responsive effector plasma cells
SSR4: Translocon-associated protein delta subunit; essential for co-translational insertion of signal peptide-containing nascent chains into ER lumen
SEC11C: Signal peptidase component required for cleavage of signal peptides from IGHG nascent chains during translocation
FKBP11: Peptidyl-prolyl cis/trans isomerase localised to ER lumen; catalyses proline isomerisation critical for immunoglobulin domain folding and heavy-light chain interaction
IGKC: Kappa light chain; co-regulated with heavy chains to maintain stoichiometric Ig assembly
XBP1: Spliced XBP1 activates UPR target genes and coordinates ER capacity expansion; present but not dominantly activated (suggests baseline UPR tone rather than acute stress)
HERPUD1: ERAD component; manages misfolded/aggregated Ig species during transit
suggested_validation: Co-immunoprecipitation of FKBP11 with newly synthesised IGHG3 heavy chains pulse-labelled with heavy isotope amino acids; measure proline isomerisation kinetics on recombinant IgG3 construct ± FKBP11 inhibitor FK506 to quantify folding enhancement

programme_name: IgLambda light chain ER quality control
functional_description: Plasma cells expressing IGLC3 (lambda light chain) engage coordinated ER proteostasis involving signal peptidase-mediated translocon translocation (SEC11C, SSR4), prolyl isomerase-catalysed folding (FKBP11, FKBP2), and selective ERAD of misfolded immunoglobulin via ER lectins (ERLEC1) and derlin retrotranslocases (DERL3). XBP1 coordinates transcriptional induction of the entire ER chaperone and quality control machinery (CRELD2, SDF2L1, PRDX4) to maintain secretory capacity in high-rate Ig-secreting plasma cells.
key_evidence: IGLC3: Lambda light chain diagnostic marker—directly indicative of IgLambda isotype identity
SEC11C: Signal peptidase catalyses co-translational removal of signal peptide from nascent Ig light chain; essential for translocon-mediated ER translocation
SSR4: Translocon-associated protein delta subunit integrates Ig chain insertion into ER lumen during translation
XBP1: IRE1α-activated spliced XBP1s transcription factor directly upregulates ER chaperones and ERAD components; rate-limiting in plasma cell UPR
FKBP11, FKBP2: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerases accelerate prolyl cis-trans isomerisation during immunoglobulin folding, preventing proline-rich domain misfolding
ERLEC1: ER-resident lectin recognises N-glycans on misfolded Ig; gates ERAD substrate selection
DERL3: Derlin-family retrotranslocase extracts ERAD-targeted misfolded Ig from ER membrane for proteasomal degradation
CRELD2: Calcium-binding protein with protein disulfide isomerase activity stabilises Ig disulphide bond formation
SDF2L1: ER chaperone cofactor binds misfolded client proteins; directly prevents Ig aggregation
PRDX4: ER-resident peroxiredoxin maintains reducing/oxidising environment for disulphide bond catalysis
suggested_validation: Sort IGLC3+ plasma cells by IGLC3 expression intensity; perform live-cell ER stress imaging (CHOP-GFP) ± XBP1 knockdown to confirm XBP1-dependent upregulation of SEC11C, ERLEC1, and DERL3 correlates with Ig secretion rate; validate by quantitative proteomics of Ig-associated ERAD substrates in IGLC3+ vs IGLC1+ sorted cells.

programme_name: IgG2 ER translocation and misfolded protein quality control
functional_description: This programme represents IgG2-secreting plasma cells undergoing active immunoglobulin synthesis with prominent ER quality control. The coordinated expression of translocon components (SSR4, SEC11C), peptidyl-prolyl isomerases (FKBP11, FKBP2), and ERAD machinery (HERPUD1) indicates robust ER-associated degradation of misfolded IgG heavy chains, while XBP1 transcription factor activation drives compensatory ER chaperone and ERAD gene expression to maintain proteostasis during high-rate Ig secretion.
key_evidence: IGHG2: IgG2 heavy chain, diagnostic of IgG-subclass switched plasma cell commitment
SSR4: Translocon-associated protein delta subunit mediating nascent IgG2 translocation across ER membrane
SEC11C: Signal peptidase C catalysing signal peptide cleavage during IgG2 translocation and processing
FKBP11 & FKBP2: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerases essential for proline-rich disulphide-bonded Ig domain folding
HERPUD1: ERAD ubiquitin ligase adaptor; induced by XBP1 to degrade misfolded IgG2 heavy chains
XBP1: UPR transcription factor; master regulator of ER chaperone and ERAD gene programmes in plasma cells
PRDX4: ER-localised peroxiredoxin providing redox homeostasis during disulphide bond formation in Ig folding
MZB1: Plasma cell-restricted protein promoting IgG secretion through cytoplasmic trafficking
suggested_validation: Perform XBP1s ChIP-seq on sorted IgG2+ plasma cells to confirm direct XBP1 binding to promoters of HERPUD1, FKBP11, SSR4 and SEC11C; validate with RT-qPCR after XBP1 knockout or ATF6α inhibition.

programme_name: IgA heavy chain ER translocation and disulfide isomerase
functional_description: This programme coordinates the early secretory pathway steps for IgA plasma cells, specifically encompassing signal peptide cleavage during co-translational translocation (SSR4, SEC11C) and prolyl isomerization of immunoglobulin heavy chain domains (FKBP11, FKBP2, CRELD2). The enrichment of ER-resident protein disulfide isomerases and chaperones reflects the intense demand for correct heavy chain folding before complex assembly with light chains, characteristic of high-titer IgA-secreting cells.
key_evidence: IGHA1: Diagnostic IgA heavy chain constant region; its selective upregulation over other isotypes defines this as IgA-specific translocation programme
SSR4: Core translocon component; mediates co-translational translocation of IgA heavy chain signal peptide
SEC11C: Signal peptidase C; processes signal peptide cleavage during IgA heavy chain entry into ER lumen
FKBP11/FKBP2: Prolyl isomerases essential for correct folding of immunoglobulin domains with multiple prolines; diagnostic of active heavy chain folding
CRELD2: ER-resident protein disulfide isomerase with calcium-binding; catalyzes inter- and intra-chain disulfide bond formation in IgA
MANF: ER-localized cytoprotective chaperone; prevents ER stress during massive Ig synthesis
DAD1: OST48 subunit of oligosaccharyltransferase complex; mediates N-linked glycosylation of IgA constant regions during translocation
suggested_validation: Perform single-molecule tracking of IGHA1-mRNA to ER-bound ribosomes in IgA+ plasma cells vs IgG+ plasma cells, quantifying co-translational translocation efficiency and FKBP11/CRELD2 recruitment kinetics via live-cell imaging with fluorescently-tagged chaperones.

programme_name: IgLambda light chain ER quality control
functional_description: This programme coordinates the biosynthesis and ER quality control of immunoglobulin lambda light chains in plasma cells. It combines signal peptide processing (SEC11C), proline isomerization (FKBP11, FKBP2) for proper Ig folding, translocon function (SSR4), and ERAD activation (HERPUD1) to manage misfolded light chain burden. The enrichment of XBP1, ER chaperones (CRELD2), and redox enzymes (PRDX4) indicates active UPR signalling to sustain high-volume secretion.
key_evidence: IGLC3: Diagnostic lambda light chain gene; its enrichment as rank-1 identifies the lambda-restricted secretion programme
SEC11C: Signal peptidase essential for processing lambda precursor signal peptides during cotranslational translocation
FKBP11 & FKBP2: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerases critical for rapid Ig folding to prevent aggregation during high-rate synthesis
XBP1: Master UPR transcription factor activated by ER stress during Ig lambda synthesis; drives ER chaperones and ERAD
HERPUD1: ERAD ubiquitin ligase adaptor; marks misfolded lambda chains for proteasomal degradation
SSR4: Translocon delta subunit; essential for stable Ig translocation across ER membrane
CRELD2: ER-resident protein disulfide isomerase; essential for disulfide bond formation in Ig lambda
PRDX4: ER-localised antioxidant; prevents aberrant disulfide bonding and aggregation during folding stress
suggested_validation: Sort plasma cells by IGLC3 vs IGLK expression and perform quantitative proteomics (TMT) ± IgLambda-specific immunoprecipitation to confirm coordinate induction of SEC11C, FKBP11/2, and HERPUD1 specifically in lambda-secreting cells, with XBP1s splicing analysis to confirm UPR activation.

programme_name: IgG heavy chain ER translocation and UPR
functional_description: This programme represents IgG-secreting plasma cells activating the canonical secretory pathway and unfolded protein response (UPR) to manage high-volume immunoglobulin synthesis. The coordinated expression of translocon components (SSR4, SEC11C), prolyl isomerase chaperones (FKBP11), XBP1-driven transcriptional activation, and ERAD machinery (HERPUD1) indicates active ER quality control during massive IgG heavy chain (IGHG1/G3/G4) and light chain (IGKC) synthesis and secretion.
key_evidence: SSR4: core translocon-associated protein complex subunit enabling co-translational translocation of signal peptide-containing Ig chains into ER lumen
IGKC + IGHG1/G3/G4: quantitatively dominant secretory proteins defining plasma cell cargo; IgG isotypes indicate class-switched, mature B cells
SEC11C: signal peptidase activity required for signal peptide cleavage during translocation of nascent heavy and light chains
FKBP11: peptidyl-prolyl isomerase essential for proper disulfide bond-dependent folding of Ig constant domains in ER
XBP1: IRE1α-activated transcription factor driving expression of ER chaperones and ERAD components in response to Ig-induced ER stress
HERPUD1: ERAD E3 ligase adaptor marking misfolded Ig for proteasomal degradation, preventing ER lumen congestion
PRDX4: ER-resident antioxidant managing ROS generated during high-rate disulfide bond formation in Ig synthesis
suggested_validation: Sort IgG+ vs IgKappa+ plasma cells by FACS; perform RT-qPCR for IRE1α splicing of XBP1 mRNA (unspliced vs spliced forms) and measure HERPUD1/PRDX4 expression; confirm ER stress activation by measuring BiP/GRP78 and ATF4 levels in IgG-high cells.

programme_name: ER translocon and chaperone-mediated Ig folding
functional_description: This programme reflects the core ER protein synthesis and quality control machinery specifically upregulated in plasma cells during active immunoglobulin secretion. SSR4 (translocon delta subunit), SEC11C (signal peptidase), and FKBP11/FKBP2 (peptidyl-prolyl isomerases) drive co-translational translocation and proline-rich domain folding of nascent Ig heavy and light chains. HSP90B1 and ERLEC1 support ER-resident chaperone networks and N-glycan-dependent quality control checkpoints essential for Ig folding fidelity.
key_evidence: SSR4: Translocon-associated protein complex delta subunit; diagnostic for active protein translocation across ER membrane during Ig synthesis
SEC11C: Signal peptidase catalysing cleavage of Ig signal peptides; rate-limiting for ER entry of both heavy and light chains
FKBP11/FKBP2: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerases accelerating proline-rich domain folding; Ig heavy/light chains contain multiple proline residues requiring PPIase activity
HSP90B1: ER-resident molecular chaperone; maintains Ig domain stability and prevents misfolding during synthesis
ERLEC1: ER lectin recognising N-glycans on Ig; couples glycan-dependent quality control to folding checkpoint
IGHA1: IgA heavy chain constant region; confirms IgA-secreting plasma cell subtype
suggested_validation: Pulse-chase SILAC proteomics combined with ER-lumen IP of FKBP11/HSP90B1 to quantify co-translational Ig folding kinetics and identify newly-synthesised heavy/light chain substrates in IgA+ plasma cells.

programme_name: IgA plasma cell ER translocation and quality control
functional_description: This programme represents IgA-secreting plasma cells with active ER translocation machinery and protein quality control systems. The signature combines JCHAIN (IgA-specific J chain), IGKC (kappa light chain), translocon components (SSR4, SEC11C), and ER-resident chaperones/isomerases (FKBP11, FKBP2, MZB1) that mediate co-translational translocation and prolyl isomerization of immunoglobulin domains. XBP1 activation indicates UPR engagement to support high-volume Ig secretion, whilst UBE2J1 and oxidative stress responses (PRDX4) manage misfolded protein clearance.
key_evidence: JCHAIN: Diagnostic of IgA plasma cells; J chain enables IgA dimer assembly and transcytosis
IGKC: Kappa light chain paired with JCHAIN indicates IgA(kappa) subtype specificity
SSR4: Translocon-associated protein; essential for co-translational translocation of Ig heavy and light chains into ER lumen
SEC11C: Signal peptidase required for cleavage of signal peptides during Ig translocation
FKBP11/FKBP2: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerases that catalyse proline cis-trans isomerization in Ig constant domains for proper folding
XBP1: Master UPR transcription factor; activated by ER stress from high Ig load to induce ER chaperones
MZB1: ER-resident chaperone in plasma cells; stabilises and facilitates Ig polymer formation
UBE2J1: E2 ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme; mediates ERAD of terminally misfolded Ig species
PRDX4: ER-localised peroxiredoxin; manages oxidative stress from disulphide bond formation in Ig
suggested_validation: Quantify JCHAIN and IGKC protein co-expression by flow cytometry in SSR4+ plasma cells; use electron microscopy to visualise dilated ER cisternae and ribosome-studded RER; measure XBP1s splicing by RT-qPCR to confirm UPR activation state

programme_name: IgG ER translocation and ERAD quality control
functional_description: This programme coordinates co-translational translocation of IgG heavy chains (IGHG1/IGHG3) via the Sec61 translocon (SSR4, SEC11C) with ER-resident quality control, specifically ERAD-mediated clearance of misfolded immunoglobulins via derlin-family retrotranslocation (DERL3, HERPUD1). FKBP11/FKBP2 peptidyl-prolyl isomerases facilitate productive IgG folding, while XBP1 transcriptional regulation sustains the ER stress response necessary for high-capacity Ig synthesis.
key_evidence: IGHG1/IGHG3: IgG heavy chain proteins defining this as IgG-specific, not IgA/IgE/IgM plasma cell subtype
SSR4: Translocon-associated protein delta subunit; essential for co-translational translocation of signal peptide-bearing Ig H-chains into ER lumen
SEC11C: Signal peptidase; catalyzes cleavage of signal peptides from nascent Ig H-chains post-translocation
FKBP11/FKBP2: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerases accelerating proline-rich Ig domain folding; diagnostic of active ER protein synthesis stress
XBP1: Master ER stress transcription factor; directly activates genes for translocon components and chaperones in plasma cells
DERL3/HERPUD1: ERAD effectors; specifically recognize and target misfolded Ig for proteasomal degradation, preventing ER lumenal accumulation
MZB1: Plasma cell-restricted ER chaperone; cooperates with BiP in Ig heavy chain stabilization
suggested_validation: Co-immunoprecipitate XBP1 with DERL3 and SSR4 in primary bone marrow plasma cells; RNAi knockdown of DERL3/HERPUD1 followed by pulse-chase mass spectrometry to measure kinetics of misfolded IgG accumulation and compare to WT controls.

programme_name: IgLambda ER quality control and ERAD surveillance
functional_description: This programme represents the endoplasmic reticulum protein folding and degradation machinery specifically activated during IgLambda light chain secretion in plasma cells. The feature is driven by coordinated expression of signal peptide processing (SEC11C), peptidyl-prolyl isomerases (FKBP11, FKBP2), chaperone-mediated refolding (SDF2L1), ERAD components (ERLEC1, DERL3), and ER translocon machinery (SSR4) to manage the burden of misfolded immunoglobulin lambda chains and maintain ER homeostasis.
key_evidence: IGLC3: Diagnostic lambda light chain isotype—directly identifies the secretory immunoglobulin product being folded
SEC11C: Signal peptidase required for co-translational processing of leader peptides on nascent Ig chains entering the translocon
FKBP11 & FKBP2: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerases essential for proline-rich Ig domain folding—critical rate-limiting step in light chain maturation
SDF2L1: ER chaperone cofactor mediating refolding of transiently misfolded lambda light chains during secretory stress
ERLEC1 & DERL3: N-glycan-binding ERAD lectin and derlin family retrotranslocator—execute proteolytic clearance of irreversibly misfolded Ig
XBP1: Master ER stress response transcription factor driving UPR-mediated expansion of ER folding capacity during high-rate Ig secretion
SSR4: Translocon-associated protein delta subunit facilitating efficient co-translational translocation of signal-peptide-bearing Ig chains
suggested_validation: Co-immunofluorescence staining for IGLC3 + XBP1 spliced form (XBP1s) + CHOP in plasma cells, combined with pulse-chase analysis of IgLambda folding kinetics ± FKBP11 inhibition (using FK506 analogue) to confirm functional dependency on peptidyl-prolyl isomerase activity

programme_name: ER quality control and immunoglobulin folding
functional_description: This programme coordinates ER translocation, chaperone-mediated immunoglobulin folding, and ERAD initiation in plasma cells. It combines signal peptide processing (SEC11C), derlin-mediated protein retrotranslocation (DERL3), ER-resident chaperones (HSP90B1, FKBP11/2, SDF2L1), and oxidative quality control (PRDX4, MANF), supporting the high protein synthesis demand of antibody secretion.

DERL3: Derlin family ERAD initiator; mediates retrotranslocation of misfolded immunoglobulins for proteasomal degradation
SEC11C: Signal peptidase subunit; processes N-terminal signal peptides from nascent heavy and light chains during translocation
HSP90B1: ER-resident Hsp90 homologue; critical chaperone for stabilising partially folded Ig heavy chains during assembly
FKBP11/FKBP2: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerases; facilitate cis-trans isomerisation of proline residues in Ig disulphide bond-rich domains
SDF2L1: ER chaperone cofactor; assists refolding of client proteins including immunoglobulins in partnership with Hsp70
HERPUD1: UPR-inducible ERAD regulator; couples unfolded protein stress sensing to selective degradation of irreversibly misfolded Ig
JCHAIN: J-chain protein; enables polymeric IgA assembly, diagnostic of IgA-secreting plasma cell activity
IGLL5: Lambda-like surrogate light chain; indicates ongoing or recent B-cell receptor assembly quality control checkpoints
suggested_validation: Co-immunoprecipitation of HSP90B1 with nascent Ig heavy chains followed by LC-MS/MS to quantify the folding client repertoire and stoichiometry of FKBP and SDF2L1 interaction partners in FACS-sorted plasma cell populations

programme_name: XBP1-driven ER protein quality control IgKappa
functional_description: This programme represents plasma cells undergoing active IgKappa light chain synthesis and secretion with coordinated ER protein quality control. The signature reflects XBP1-mediated transcriptional activation of ER chaperones (FKBP11, PRDX4), translocon components (SSR4, SEC11C), and ERAD effectors (HERPUD1, ERLEC1) to manage the high flux of immunoglobulin through the secretory pathway while preventing aggregation-induced ER stress.
key_evidence: XBP1: IRE1α-activated transcription factor; the master regulator of plasma cell ER expansion and UPR-driven chaperone/ERAD gene expression
IGKC: Diagnostic IgKappa light chain; indicates kappa-restricted plasma cell population with active secretion burden
FKBP11: Prolyl isomerase essential for proper disulfide bond isomerization in nascent Ig molecules; marks active Ig folding demand
HERPUD1: ERAD ubiquitin ligase adaptor; activated by IRE1α signalling to clear misfolded Ig and prevent ER overload
SSR4: Core translocon component required for co-translational translocation of signal peptide-bearing IgKappa; rate-limiting for secretion
ERLEC1: ER lectin for N-glycan recognition; part of ERAD-Mannose6-phosphate pathway; selects misfolded glycoproteins for degradation
PRDX4: ER-resident antioxidant; prevents Ig disulfide bond-forming environment from generating ROS during high-rate secretion
suggested_validation: Perform single-cell RNA velocity on XBP1/IGKC co-expressing cells combined with ER stress reporter (e.g., ATF4-GFP or CHOP-tdTomato) FACS to confirm that high HERPUD1/ERLEC1 expression correlates with active ER-UPR signalling in kappa-secreting plasma cells, distinguishing this from lambda-restricted or non-secreting B-cell states.

programme_name: ER translocon signal peptide processing ER-secretory
functional_description: This programme represents the initial stages of immunoglobulin secretory pathway biogenesis, specifically signal peptide recognition, translocation, and co-translational processing at the ER translocon. The coordinated upregulation of translocon components (SSR4, SEC11C), peptidyl-prolyl isomerases (FKBP11, FKBP2), and disulfide bond catalysts (PDIA6, P4HB) indicates active processing of nascent Ig chains as they enter the ER lumen. This is distinct from downstream UPR responses and represents the constitutive secretory machinery operating at baseline in actively secreting plasma cells.
key_evidence: SSR4: Core translocon-associated protein complex component; mediates co-translational translocation of signal peptide-bearing nascent chains into ER lumen
SEC11C: Signal peptidase C; essential for signal peptide cleavage from nascent secretory proteins immediately post-translocation
FKBP11 & FKBP2: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerases that accelerate proline-containing peptide bond isomerization, critical for rapid Ig chain folding kinetics
PDIA6 & P4HB: ER-resident disulfide bond catalysts; P4HB is rate-limiting for Ig heavy and light chain disulfide bond formation
IGLC2: Lambda light chain constant region; direct evidence of active Ig secretion in this plasma cell population
XBP1: IRE1α-spliced form acts as transactivator of ER chaperone genes (PDIA6, P4HB) and translocon components under sustained secretory load
MZB1: ER-luminal chaperone supporting proper Ig folding and preventing aggregation during high-rate secretion
suggested_validation: Co-immunoprecipitate SSR4 and SEC11C with nascent Ig chains using pulse-labeling with methionine-35S followed by ER fractionation, or perform ribosome profiling to confirm translocon-associated ribosomes are enriched at Ig genes in this plasma cell cluster.

programme_name: IgA light chain ER translocation and proline isomerization
functional_description: This programme specifically activates IgA-secreting plasma cells and represents the initial translational phase of IgA heavy chain synthesis coupled with co-translational translocation via the SEC61 translocon (SSR4, SEC11C). The enrichment of peptidyl-prolyl isomerases (FKBP11, FKBP2) indicates specialised proline-rich region folding within IgA heavy chains, which contain abundant prolines in their hinge and constant regions. This is coupled with antioxidant priming (PRDX4) and ER redox homeostasis (HSP90B1) characteristic of the high-flux IgA secretory pathway.
key_evidence: IGHA1: Direct marker of IgA heavy chain synthesis; diagnostic for IgA-secreting plasma cells
IGLC2: IgLambda light chain paired with IgA; confirms lambda-restricted IgA subtype
SSR4: Translocon-associated protein delta subunit essential for co-translational translocation of IgA nascent chain
SEC11C: Signal peptidase complex member required for IgA signal peptide cleavage during translocation
FKBP11: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerase specialised for proline-rich IgA hinge region folding
FKBP2: Second FKBP isoform indicating sustained proline cis/trans isomerisation demand
HSP90B1: ER molecular chaperone supporting IgA heavy chain folding at high translation rates
PRDX4: ER-resident antioxidant preventing disulphide bond misfolding during rapid Ig synthesis
suggested_validation: Perform ER-lumen ribosome profiling (translatome-seq) on IGHA1+IGLC2+ plasma cells to quantify ribosome dwell times on proline-rich IgA hinge codons and validate FKBP11/FKBP2-dependent translational kinetics relative to IgG/IgM-secreting cells.

programme_name: IgLambda light chain ER translocation and quality control
functional_description: This programme mediates co-translational translocation and ER quality control of immunoglobulin lambda light chains during active plasma cell secretion. The feature is driven by IGLC2 (lambda light chain), SSR4 (translocon delta subunit), SEC11C (signal peptidase), and FKBP11/FKBP2 (prolyl isomerases) which facilitate efficient Ig chain folding and translocation across the ER membrane. XBP1 activation coordinates the transcriptional response to support high-throughput Ig synthesis while ERLEC1 and UBE2J1 enforce N-glycan-dependent quality control and ERAD of misfolded intermediates.
key_evidence: IGLC2: diagnostic marker of lambda light chain-secreting plasma cells; enables antigen binding
SSR4: delta subunit of translocon complex; essential for co-translational translocation of signal peptide-containing Ig chains
SEC11C: signal peptidase catalysing N-terminal cleavage of Ig signal peptides during translocation
FKBP11 & FKBP2: prolyl isomerases accelerating proline-rich Ig domain folding within ER lumen
XBP1: UPR-activated transcription factor driving ER chaperone and secretory capacity genes
ERLEC1: ER lectin recognising N-glycans on Ig heavy/light chains; ERAD triage factor
UBE2J1: E2 conjugase for ubiquitin-dependent proteasomal degradation of misfolded Ig
suggested_validation: Sort plasma cells by IGLC2/IGLC3 expression ratio; perform quantitative proteomics (LC-MS/MS) on ER-enriched fractions to measure IgLambda:IgKappa translocation efficiency and compare FKBP11/FKBP2-dependent folding rates using pulsed-chase pulse-labelling with radioactive methionine.

programme_name: IgG2-kappa ER translocation and prolyl isomerase chaperone
functional_description: This programme coordinates co-translational translocation and prolyl isomerisation of IgG2-kappa immunoglobulin heterodimers during secretory pathway entry. The co-occurrence of SSR4 (translocon delta subunit), SEC11C (signal peptidase), IGKC (kappa light chain), IGHG2 (IgG2 heavy chain), and FKBP11/FKBP2 (prolyl isomerases) indicates active signal peptide cleavage and peptide bond isomerisation—rate-limiting steps for efficient assembly of properly folded Ig molecules. XBP1 and HERPUD1 suggest concurrent UPR priming to sense translocation efficiency and initiate ERAD if misfolding occurs.
key_evidence: IGKC + IGHG2: specific IgG2-kappa isotype pair diagnostic of mature plasma cells
SSR4 + SEC11C: translocon and signal peptidase components required for co-translational translocation
FKBP11 + FKBP2: prolyl-prolyl cis/trans isomerases—essential for rate-limiting proline bond isomerisation in Ig folds
XBP1: UPR master regulator indicating ER stress sensing during high-rate immunoglobulin synthesis
HERPUD1: ERAD initiation factor; couples translocation quality control to protein degradation if misfolding occurs
PRDX4: ER-resident peroxiredoxin maintaining redox balance during disulphide bond formation in Ig dimers
suggested_validation: Co-immunoprecipitate SSR4 and SEC11C with FKBP11 in sorted IgG2-kappa plasma cells; monitor prolyl isomerisation kinetics of IGKC-IGHG2 heterodimers by pulse-chase mass spectrometry in cells with FKBP11/FKBP2 knockout.

programme_name: IgKappa light chain ER translocation quality control
functional_description: This programme captures the early secretory pathway events specific to IgKappa-producing plasma cells, focused on co-translational translocation of light chains across the ER membrane and initial quality control. The coordinated expression of IGKC (kappa light chain), SSR4 (translocon-associated protein delta subunit), SEC11C (signal peptidase), and FKBP11/FKBP2 (prolyl isomerases) indicates active, coupled translocation of nascent immunoglobulin chains with proline-rich folding domains. This is distinct from downstream UPR or ERAD programmes and represents the committed biosynthetic entry point for kappa-containing immunoglobulins.
key_evidence: IGKC: Diagnostic kappa light chain gene; exclusively marks this light chain isotype among plasma cell subtypes
SSR4: Translocon-associated protein complex delta subunit; essential for co-translational protein translocation into ER lumen
SEC11C: Signal peptidase; catalyzes N-terminal signal sequence cleavage immediately post-translocation, rate-limiting for light chain processing
FKBP11 & FKBP2: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerases; facilitate proper cis/trans proline isomerization during co-translational folding of Ig domains
ERLEC1: ER-resident lectin; N-glycan recognition protein for early quality control checkpoint at the ER entry gate
suggested_validation: Perform translocation kinetics assay comparing IGKC+ vs IGLC+ plasma cells: pulse-chase pulse with radioactive methionine at 37°C vs 20°C (block post-translocation folding) to demonstrate SEC11C-dependent, temperature-sensitive translocation of kappa chains specifically; co-immunoprecipitate SSR4 with nascent IGKC-ribosome complexes to confirm translocon engagement.

programme_name: IgKappa ER translocation and prolyl isomerase folding
functional_description: This programme represents the early secretory pathway specialization in kappa light chain-producing plasma cells, characterized by coordinated translocon function (SSR4, SEC11C), prolyl isomerase-mediated folding (FKBP11, FKBP2), and XBP1-driven ER chaperone transcription. The co-expression of IGKC with signal peptide processing machinery and ER oxidoreductases (PRDX4) indicates active translocation and oxidative folding of immunoglobulin chains within the ER lumen.
key_evidence: SSR4: Translocon-associated protein delta subunit—essential for co-translational translocation of IGKC across ER membrane; diagnostic of active secretory pathway engagement
IGKC: Kappa light chain constant region—sole diagnostic marker of kappa isotype specificity; must be distinguished from IGLC genes in lambda-restricted plasma cells
FKBP11: Peptidyl-prolyl cis-trans isomerase specifically enriched in ER—catalyzes prolyl isomerization critical for rapid IGKC folding; marks committed folding specialists
XBP1: Spliced XBP1 transcription factor—master regulator of ER chaperone expression (BiP, GRP94, PDI); its presence indicates active UPR-α (not ER stress) to support high-rate secretion
SEC11C: Signal peptidase complex component—essential for N-terminal signal sequence removal from nascent IGKC; diagnostic of active co-translational processing
HERPUD1: ER-resident ERAD ubiquitin ligase—manages misfolded kappa chain ERAD; indicates quality control capacity rather than ER stress state
suggested_validation: Perform phospho-flow cytometry on bone marrow plasma cells using anti-phospho-eIF2α and anti-phospho-IRE1α (UPR stress markers) vs anti-XBP1s (spliced XBP1) gating on IGKC+ cells; validate that SSR4+FKBP11+ kappa cells show XBP1s+ without eIF2α phosphorylation, confirming adapted secretion (not stress response).

programme_name: ER translocon-mediated Ig secretory pathway initiation
functional_description: This programme represents the early secretory pathway machinery required for immunoglobulin translocation across the ER membrane during plasma cell differentiation. The feature is dominated by translocon subunits (SSR4, SEC11C), ER-resident chaperones (HSP90B1, FKBP11), and IGLL5 (surrogate light chain), indicating coordinated activation of signal peptide recognition and co-translational translocation machinery. The presence of PRDX4 and HERPUD1 suggests concurrent ER redox homeostasis and UPR priming necessary for handling the high Ig secretory load in plasma cells.
key_evidence: SSR4: Translocon-associated protein (TRAP) delta subunit—rate-limiting for nascent polypeptide recognition and ER membrane targeting
SEC11C: Signal peptidase complex component—essential for signal peptide cleavage of pre-Ig molecules at the ER membrane
IGLL5: Surrogate light chain—diagnostic of early B-cell/plasma cell ER protein synthesis machinery engagement
HSP90B1: ER-localised Hsp90 homologue—obligate chaperone for Ig heavy and light chain folding during translocation
FKBP11: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerase—catalyses cis/trans isomerisation of proline residues critical for Ig domain folding
HERPUD1: UPR effector—bridges translocon function with ER-associated protein degradation (ERAD) for quality control
PRDX4: ER-localised peroxiredoxin—maintains reducing ER environment essential for disulphide bond formation in Ig constant domains
suggested_validation: Perform ER-targeted photocrosslinking assay in plasma cells with radioactive-labelled nascent Ig heavy chain to directly visualise SSR4/translocon occupancy; combine with pulse-chase secretion kinetics to confirm rate-limiting step in translocation.

programme_name: IgA heavy chain ER translocation and chaperone folding
functional_description: This programme captures the early secretory pathway specialization in IgA-secreting plasma cells, characterized by coordinated upregulation of translocon components (SSR4, SEC11C) and prolyl isomerases (FKBP11, FKBP2) that facilitate co-translational translocation and proline-rich heavy chain folding. XBP1 and HSP90B1 co-activation indicates initiation of the unfolded protein response coupled with ER chaperone induction to manage the high folding demand of IgA polymeric complexes.
key_evidence: IGHA1: IgA heavy chain gene—defines the immunoglobulin isotype and confirms IgA-secreting plasma cell identity
SSR4: Translocon-associated protein delta subunit—essential for co-translational translocation of signal peptide-containing immunoglobulins into ER lumen
SEC11C: Signal peptidase I catalytic subunit—processes N-terminal signal peptides during translocation of nascent heavy chains
FKBP11 & FKBP2: Prolyl isomerases—catalyze cis-trans isomerization of proline residues abundant in immunoglobulin constant regions to accelerate folding kinetics
XBP1: UPR transcription factor—activates downstream ER chaperones (HSP90B1, MANF) and ERAD components in response to heavy chain load
HSP90B1: ER-resident chaperone (GRP94)—assists IgA heavy chain folding and quaternary complex assembly with light chains
MZB1: ER-resident immunoglobulin chaperone—facilitates IgA dimer/polymer formation and prevents aggregation
suggested_validation: Immunoprecipitate XBP1-bound chromatin from IgA+ plasma cells (ChIP-seq) and correlate XBP1 occupancy at HSP90B1/FKBP11/SEC11C promoters with single-cell IgA expression intensity; validate by blocking SEC11C or FKBP11 activity and measuring IgA secretion capacity and ER stress markers (ATF4, CHOP).

programme_name: ER chaperone-mediated Ig folding and ERAD coordination
functional_description: This programme coordinates ER-resident protein folding machinery (FKBP11, FKBP2, PDIA6, SDF2L1) with signal peptide processing (SEC11C, SSR4) and ERAD surveillance (HERPUD1, ERLEC1) to maintain proteostasis during active immunoglobulin synthesis. XBP1 acts as the master regulator of this integrated ER quality control response, while oxidative stress management (PRDX4) protects nascent disulfide bonds in Ig molecules.
key_evidence: XBP1: IRE1α-dependent transcription factor that drives ER chaperone and ERAD gene expression during plasma cell differentiation
FKBP11, FKBP2: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerases essential for proline-rich Ig fold maturation
PDIA6: ER-resident protein disulfide isomerase catalysing Ig heavy/light chain disulfide bond formation
SEC11C, SSR4: Signal peptidase and translocon subunit coordinating co-translational translocation of Ig chains
HERPUD1, ERLEC1: ERAD initiation factors recognising misfolded Ig for proteasomal degradation
SDF2L1: ER chaperone cofactor stabilising partially folded Ig intermediates
PRDX4: ER-localised peroxiredoxin protecting Ig disulfide bonds from oxidative damage
suggested_validation: Co-immunoprecipitate XBP1s with HERPUD1 and PDIA6 in sorted plasma cells; measure ER stress kinetics (eIF2α phosphorylation, ATF4 induction) following transient XBP1 knockdown using flow cytometry and immunoblotting of CD138+ cells from bone marrow.

programme_name: IgG heavy chain ER translocation and proline isomerization
functional_description: This programme represents the early secretory pathway commitment of IgG-secreting plasma cells, characterised by robust signal peptide-dependent translocation (SSR4, SEC11C) and peptidyl-prolyl cis-trans isomerisation of proline-rich IgG heavy chain domains (FKBP11). The coordinated expression of IGHG1, IGKC with translocon machinery and prolyl isomerase activity indicates active co-translational translocation and post-translational folding of IgG molecules entering the ER lumen, prior to downstream chaperone-mediated quality control.
key_evidence: IGHG1: IgG heavy chain—diagnostic for IgG isotype plasma cells; upstream of translocation and ER folding
SSR4: Translocon-associated protein complex delta subunit; essential for signal peptide-dependent translocation of nascent heavy chain
SEC11C: Signal peptidase component; directly processes signal peptides during co-translational translocation of IGHG1
FKBP11: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerase; catalyses folding of proline-rich IgG heavy chain domains critical for structural stability
IGKC: Kappa light chain; paired with IGHG1, validates mature secretory phenotype
PDIA6: ER disulfide isomerase; supports disulfide bond formation during co-translational folding
suggested_validation: Ribosome profiling or selective ribosome IP (RIP-seq) on IGHG1+ plasma cells to confirm co-translational translocation and calculate IGHG1 polysome density; immunoprecipitate FKBP11-IGHG1 complexes to validate prolyl isomerisation of heavy chain in situ.

programme_name: IgLambda light chain ER folding quality control
functional_description: This programme specifically coordinates ER translocation, signal peptide processing, and chaperone-mediated folding of lambda light chain immunoglobulins in plasma cells. The feature integrates translocon assembly (SSR4, SEC11C), prolyl-isomerase catalysts (FKBP11, FKBP2) for proline-rich immunoglobulin domains, and XBP1-responsive ER quality control machinery (ERLEC1) to ensure proper IgLambda maturation before secretion.
key_evidence: IGLC2: diagnostic marker—directly encodes lambda light chain protein uniquely identifying this isotype-restricted programme
SSR4: translocon-associated protein delta subunit—essential co-translational translocation machinery for nascent Ig chains across ER membrane
FKBP11/FKBP2: peptidyl-prolyl isomerases—catalyse rate-limiting proline cis/trans isomerisation endemic to Ig constant and variable domains
SEC11C: signal peptidase—processes N-terminal signal sequences from nascent light chains, prerequisite for ER entry and proper folding topology
XBP1: ATF6/IRE1-activated transcription factor—orchestrates ER chaperone and ERAD machinery expansion during Ig production stress response
ERLEC1: N-glycan-dependent ER quality control—recognises misfolded Ig glycoproteins for ERAD targeting, preventing secretion of aggregation-prone intermediates
suggested_validation: Perform isotype-resolved proteomic quantification (LC-MS/MS with isotope labelling) of IgLambda vs IgKappa light chain assembly kinetics in primary plasma cells ±XBP1 inhibition; correlate transcript levels of FKBP11, ERLEC1 and IGLC2 using single-molecule FISH to confirm coordinated expression within individual plasma cells

programme_name: IgG heavy chain ER translocation and disulfide isomerization
functional_description: This programme specifically drives the co-translational translocation and initial folding of IgG heavy chains (IGHG1, IGHG3) across the ER membrane via the translocon complex (SSR4, SEC11C). The programme is dominated by ER-resident disulfide isomerases (PDIA6, FKBP11, FKBP2) and prolyl isomerases that catalyse the oxidative folding and domain-specific disulfide bond formation required for immunoglobulin tertiary structure, prior to downstream quality control and secretion.
key_evidence: IGHG1, IGHG3: IgG heavy chain cargo proteins requiring co-translational translocation and oxidative folding with multiple disulfide bonds
SSR4: δ-subunit of translocon-associated protein (TRAP) complex; essential for co-translational translocation of signal peptide-bearing IGHG nascent chains
SEC11C: Signal peptidase C that cleaves signal peptides during ER translocation; diagnostic of active translocation machinery
PDIA6, FKBP11, FKBP2: Disulfide isomerases and prolyl isomerases catalysing oxidative folding and cis-trans isomerization of proline-rich IGHG domains
XBP1: IRE1α-spliced transcription factor driving expression of ER chaperones and oxidoreductases during IgG secretory load
HERPUD1: ERAD component upregulated by XBP1-driven UPR to clear misfolded IGHG substrates
suggested_validation: Pulse-chase with 35S-methionine on purified plasma cells ± PDIA6 small molecule inhibitor (e.g. bacitracin), followed by non-reducing SDS-PAGE and autoradiography to quantify IGHG disulfide formation kinetics and accumulation of misfolded intermediates

programme_name: IgA ER translocation and chaperone-mediated folding
functional_description: This programme coordinates the signal peptide-dependent translocation of IgA heavy chains into the endoplasmic reticulum via the translocon (SSR4, SEC11C), followed by prolyl isomerase-catalysed folding of proline-rich immunoglobulin domains (FKBP11, FKBP2). HSP90B1 and MZB1 provide ATP-dependent ER chaperone support and quality control scaffolding to prevent aggregation of the large IgA polymer, while XBP1 drives sustained expression of ER-resident folding machinery under the burden of high-rate secretion.
key_evidence: IGHA1: IgA heavy chain; diagnostic marker of IgA-secreting plasma cells
SSR4: Translocon-associated protein delta subunit; essential for co-translational translocation of signal peptide-bearing Ig chains
SEC11C: Signal peptidase I catalytic subunit; cleaves Ig signal peptides immediately upon translocation
FKBP11 & FKBP2: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerases; catalyse cis-trans isomerisation of proline residues abundant in Ig constant regions
HSP90B1: ER-resident ATP-dependent chaperone; prevents misfolding and aggregation of nascent IgA polymers
MZB1: Marginal zone B-cell marker with ER localisation; acts as Ig assembly checkpoint and quality control adaptor
XBP1: IRE1-activated UPR transcription factor; drives expression of ER chaperones in response to Ig secretion load
suggested_validation: Immunofluorescence co-localisation of IGHA1 with SEC11C and HSP90B1 in ER/Golgi compartments of bone marrow plasma cells, combined with surface plasmon resonance or yeast two-hybrid to confirm physical interaction between MZB1 and IgA polymers

functional_description: This programme represents the early-to-basophilic erythroid differentiation stage characterized by active mitochondrial bioenergetics and iron metabolism. The dominant expression of ATP synthase subunits (ATP5IF1, ATP5MF, ATP5MC1) alongside NADH dehydrogenase components (NDUFS5, UQCRQ) indicates robust oxidative phosphorylation capacity required for rapid haem synthesis. Coordinated upregulation of iron handling (FTH1, AHSP) and antioxidant defences (SOD1, PRDX2) reflects the metabolic demands of early erythropoiesis where haem-globin assembly necessitates intensive iron utilization and ROS management.
key_evidence: ATP5IF1, ATP5MF, ATP5MC1: ATP synthase subunits diagnostic of active mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation in energy-demanding early erythroblasts
NDUFS5, UQCRQ: Complex I and III respiratory chain components required to sustain OXPHOS for haem and globin synthesis
FTH1: Iron storage capacity essential for haem biosynthesis; AHSP: α-globin chaperone preventing precipitation during haemoglobin assembly
SOD1, PRDX2: Antioxidant enzymes protecting against ROS generated by high metabolic flux and iron metabolism
BLVRB: Final step heme catabolism, indicating active haem turnover; HMGB1: stress response/apoptosis regulator in metabolically active cells
suggested_validation: Co-stain pro-erythroblasts and basophilic erythroblasts with MitoTracker Red (mitochondrial mass/membrane potential), CALCEIN-AM (labile iron pool), and TMRM to demonstrate that ATP5IF1/ATP synthase-high cells exhibit increased oxidative phosphorylation capacity and iron flux relative to downstream polychromatic/orthochromatic stages where mitochondria are degraded.

programme_name: Pro-erythroblast ribosomal protein synthesis
functional_description: This programme represents the early pro-erythroblast stage characterized by intense ribosomal biogenesis and translational machinery assembly. The dominant expression of ribosomal proteins (RPS/RPL genes) and translation factors (EEF1B2, PPIA) reflects the massive protein synthetic demand required for haemoglobin accumulation and cell proliferation. PTMA and YBX1 provide anti-apoptotic support and RNA chaperoning during this metabolically demanding differentiation phase.

EEF1B2: translation elongation factor essential for high-throughput protein synthesis capacity
PTMA: prolines-rich nucleoprotein that suppresses apoptosis during the energetically costly pro-erythroblast proliferative phase
YBX1: cold-shock domain protein that regulates mRNA stability and translation initiation under biosynthetic stress
MT-CO3: oxidative phosphorylation component supporting ATP generation for anabolic demands
suggested_validation: Perform polysome profiling on sorted pro-erythroblasts vs mature erythroblasts to quantify ribosome loading and nascent protein synthesis rates, combined with pulse-labeling of haemoglobin synthesis

programme_name: Early erythroid oxidative phosphorylation metabolic priming
functional_description: This programme represents early-stage erythroid progenitors (pro-erythroblasts and basophilic erythroblasts) during the critical transition from proliferation to differentiation, characterized by activation of mitochondrial bioenergetics machinery. NDUFS5 & UQCRQ: Complex I and III OXPHOS subunits confirming mitochondrial respiratory chain maturation preceding haemoglobin production phase
YBX1: Cold shock domain protein involved in mRNA stability and translation regulation during erythroid cell cycle arrest and differentiation commitment
SOD1: Superoxide dismutase upregulation indicates oxidative stress management in high-metabolic-rate early erythroid cells with active OXPHOS

programme_name: Early erythroid mitochondrial bioenergetics and heme synthesis
functional_description: This programme represents early-stage erythroid differentiation (pro-erythroblast to basophilic erythroblast) characterized by intense mitochondrial ATP synthesis capacity and heme biosynthesis infrastructure. PRDX2: peroxiredoxin antioxidant essential for managing oxidative stress from haem and iron metabolism
suggested_validation: Perform metabolic flux analysis (Seahorse) comparing early erythroblasts (pro- and basophilic stages) vs mature stages, measuring ATP production rate and oxygen consumption to validate mitochondrial bioenergetic dependency; correlate with intracellular iron and heme quantification across differentiation stages.

programme_name: Early erythroid mitochondrial oxidative metabolism

NDUFS5, UQCRQ: Complex I and III components of electron transport chain, diagnostic of cells with high mitochondrial energy demand
FTH1, BLVRB: Iron storage and haem catabolism/recycling; FTH1 is particularly elevated in early erythroid progenitors managing iron for haemoglobin synthesis

HMGB1, YBX1, PCLAF: Chromatin remodelling and transcriptional regulators supporting the massive upregulation of erythroid-specific genes
