Concurrent upregulation of mitochondrial electron transport chain components (MT-CO2, MT-CO3) and iron storage (FTH1) reflects the coordination of oxidative phosphorylation with iron metabolism during early erythroid commitment, when cells establish the biosynthetic machinery and metabolic capacity required for terminal differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS17, RPL37A, RPS24, RPLP0, RPS23, RPL4, RPL7A: Multiple ribosomal proteins (40S and 60S subunits) indicate active ribosome biogenesis as hallmark of early erythroblast translational demand
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor reflects high-throughput protein synthesis required for haemoglobin accumulation
MT-CO3, MT-CO2: Cytochrome oxidase subunits establish mitochondrial ATP generation needed to power ribosome assembly and haemoglobin synthesis
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain coordinates iron storage with translational readiness, preventing iron-induced oxidative stress during massive haem synthesis
YBX1, PTMA, HMGB1: RNA/DNA-binding proteins regulate ribosomal gene expression and protect against apoptosis during this biosynthetically intensive phase
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry sort of CD71+ CD45- cells stratified by surface transferrin receptor (CD71) levels and perform pulse-chase metabolic labelling (35S-methionine incorporation + seahorse mitochondrial stress test) to quantify translation rates and oxidative capacity across pro-erythroblast and basophilic erythroblast stages.

programme_name: Early erythroid mitochondrial oxidative metabolism
functional_description: This feature marks pro-erythroblasts and CFU-E early progenitors with active mitochondrial OXPHOS (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-ND5, UQCRH) coupled to robust protein synthesis machinery (RPS/RPL genes, EEF1B2, PPIA). This metabolic state supports the intensive haem biosynthesis and globin chain production required during early erythroid commitment, before the terminal maturation phases that progressively silence mitochondrial function.
key_evidence: MT-CO2/CO3/ND1/ND5: cytochrome oxidase and NADH dehydrogenase subunits diagnostic of active OXPHOS in metabolically demanding pro-erythroblasts
RPS23/24/17, RPL37A/7A, RPLP0: co-enrichment of 40S and 60S ribosomal subunits indicates global translation capacity required for massive globin synthesis
UQCRH: ubiquinol-cytochrome-c reductase subunit confirms active mitochondrial electron transport chain, essential for ATP generation and haem-biosynthetic cofactors
suggested_validation: Perform seahorse metabolic profiling (oxygen consumption rate / extracellular acidification rate) on FACs-sorted pro-erythroblasts vs basophilic erythroblasts to quantify OXPHOS decline during maturation; correlate with feature activation trajectory

programme_name: Pro-erythroblast oxidative phosphorylation and proliferation
functional_description: This programme marks early-stage pro-erythroblasts undergoing rapid proliferation with elevated mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation capacity. The co-enrichment of OXPHOS subunits (MT-CO2/3, MT-ND1/5, NDUFS5, UQCRQ), ribosomal proteins (RPL37A), iron homeostasis mediators (TFR2), and cell cycle regulators (GADD45GIP1) indicates metabolically active cells with high energy demand and protein synthesis rates required for massive haemoglobin accumulation and rapid division.
key_evidence: MT-CO2/3, MT-ND1/5, NDUFS5, UQCRQ: Core OXPHOS Complex I-IV subunits diagnostic of mitochondrial bioenergetic activation in proliferating erythroblasts
TFR2: Iron-responsive transferrin receptor essential for iron uptake supporting haem synthesis and cytochrome oxidase assembly
RPL37A: Ribosomal protein reflecting elevated translation machinery for rapid globin chain synthesis
GADD45GIP1: Cell cycle inhibitor suggesting G1/S checkpoint control typical of pro-erythroblast expansion phase
S100A6, HMGB1, PTMA: Calcium signalling and apoptosis suppression consistent with survival of metabolically stressed proliferating cells
suggested_validation: Co-stain pro-erythroblasts (CD71+CD235a-) for MitoTracker Deep Red and BrdU incorporation to confirm elevated mitochondrial content and S-phase entry correlate with OXPHOS gene expression signature

prior_zero_shot_name: Ribosome biogenesis in proliferating erythroid progenitors
programme_name: Ribosomal protein synthesis in proliferating erythroid progenitors
functional_description: This feature marks the early erythroid progenitor compartment (Pro-Erythroblasts and CFU-E; 54% of activating cells) during active ribosome biogenesis and protein synthesis. The dominant signature comprises 40S and 60S ribosomal protein subunits (RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0) coupled with translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) and nucleolar assembly factors (FBL), reflecting the massive translational demand for haemoglobin synthesis machinery assembly. Supporting metabolic genes (GAPDH, LDHB) and chromatin regulators (HMGN1, H2AFZ) indicate concurrent DNA replication and transcriptional activation characteristic of the G1/S-phase transition in erythroid progenitors.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4: Diagnostic multi-subunit ribosomal protein co-expression essential for 40S/60S ribosome assembly—indicates active ribosome biogenesis rather than general protein synthesis
FBL: Nucleolar fibrillarin marks the nucleolar biogenesis compartment where ribosomal assembly occurs, specifically elevated in cycling progenitors
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor reinforces active translational engagement; critical for rapid globin chain synthesis initiation
GAPDH + LDHB: Glycolytic and lactate metabolism markers reflect the aerobic metabolism of rapidly dividing erythroid progenitors preparing for haemoglobinization
suggested_validation: Quantify ribosomal protein mRNA and mature 18S/28S rRNA abundance by qRT-PCR and Northern blot in FACS-sorted Pro-Erythroblasts vs. Basophilic Erythroblasts to confirm the biogenesis programme is downregulated post-proliferation during terminal maturation.

programme_name: Early erythroid translation and iron homeostasis
functional_description: This programme captures the early erythroid differentiation stage (pro-erythroblasts and basophilic erythroblasts) characterized by intensive ribosomal biogenesis and protein synthesis capacity, coupled with iron storage management via ferritin. The coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (RPS/RPL), translation factors (EEF1B2), and iron metabolism (FTH1) reflects the massive translational machinery buildup required for haemoglobin production, while YBX1 coordinates mRNA stability during this anabolic phase.
key_evidence: YBX1: Y-box binding protein acts as global translational regulator and mRNA stabilizer during rapid protein synthesis in early erythroid cells
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain essential for managing labile iron pool during haemoglobin synthesis—diagnostic of iron-loaded early erythroblasts
RPS17/RPS2/RPS23/RPL4/RPL7A/RPLP0: Coordinated ribosomal protein upregulation indicates ribosomal biogenesis surge specific to early erythroid stages
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor reflects active translational capacity needed for globin chain synthesis
MT-CO3: Mitochondrial oxidoreductase suggests elevated oxidative phosphorylation supporting ATP demand of anabolic erythropoiesis
suggested_validation: Perform polysome profiling on sorted pro-erythroblasts vs basophilic erythroblasts to quantify translational activity and correlate with SAE feature activation intensity across the erythroid differentiation trajectory

programme_name: Pro-erythroblast ribosomal synthesis and mitochondrial bioenergetics
functional_description: This programme captures the early erythroid commitment phase (76.5% pro-erythroblasts) characterized by coordinated upregulation of cytoplasmic ribosomal protein genes (RPS17, RPS23, RPS24, RPL37A, RPL4, RPL7A, RPLP0) supporting massive haemoglobin synthesis, coupled with concurrent mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation genes (MT-CO3, MT-CO2, MT-ND1, UQCRH). This metabolic integration reflects the high ATP and protein synthetic demands of pro-erythroblasts before terminal differentiation triggers mitochondrial autophagy.
key_evidence: RPS17/RPS23/RPS24/RPL37A/RPL7A/RPL4: Coordinate 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit proteins diagnostic of translational machinery upscaling in proliferative pro-erythroblasts
MT-CO3/MT-CO2/MT-ND1/UQCRH: Mitochondrial Complex I, II, III, IV structural/catalytic subunits indicating sustained oxidative phosphorylation for ATP during active erythroid proliferation

EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor reflecting ongoing protein synthesis capacity; HNRNPA1/YBX1: RNA-binding proteins coordinating mRNA processing and stability during high-volume haemoglobin transcription
suggested_validation: Co-immunofluorescence for CD34+GPA- pro-erythroblasts co-stained with anti-RPS17 (ribosome marker) and TMRM/JC-1 (mitochondrial membrane potential indicator) to confirm bioenergetic coupling; or polysome profiling to quantify translational activity in FACS-sorted pro-erythroblasts vs. basophilic erythroblasts

programme_name: Ribosomal protein synthesis in erythroid-committed progenitors
functional_description: This feature marks a proliferative state dominated by CFU-E (30.5%) and cycling progenitors (27%), characterized by coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (RPS2, RPS17, RPS23, RPS24, RPL4, RPL7A, RPL37A, RPLP0) and translation elongation factors (EEF1B2). The presence of LDHB and GAPDH alongside ribosomal machinery indicates concurrent glycolytic engagement to fuel rapid protein synthesis during erythroid differentiation, particularly at the CFU-E→early erythroblast transition where haemoglobin synthesis begins.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS2, RPS23, RPS17, RPLP0, RPL7A, RPL37A, RPL4: Coordinated 40S/60S subunit components diagnostic of active ribosomal biogenesis—required for the massive globin chain synthesis demand in CFU-E expansion
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor indicating active protein synthesis machinery, not just ribosome assembly
LDHB + GAPDH: Glycolytic enzymes coupling energy metabolism to protein synthesis; consistent with the metabolic intensification of erythroid commitment
NPM1: Nucleolar phosphoprotein essential for ribosome assembly and centrosome regulation, supporting active cell division in cycling progenitors
suggested_validation: Sort top 200 feature-positive cells by flow cytometry (CD34+CD71+CD45RA− to identify CFU-E/early erythroblasts) and perform polysome profiling or 35S-labeling to confirm active translation rate exceeds baseline haematopoietic cells.

prior_zero_shot_name: Early erythroblast translational and metabolic activation
programme_name: Pro-erythroblast ribosomal translation and iron metabolism
functional_description: This programme represents early-stage erythroid progenitors (64% Pro-Erythroblasts) engaged in intensive ribosomal biogenesis and protein synthesis required for haemoglobin production. Simultaneous upregulation of iron storage (FTH1) and nucleotide metabolism (NME4) reflects coordinated preparation for massive haem synthesis and rapid cell division. The prominence of translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) and RNA-binding proteins (YBX1, HNRNPA1) indicates active translational control during the proliferative phase of erythroid differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS2, RPL4, RPLP0, RPS23, RPL37A, RPL7A: >40% of top 15 genes are ribosomal proteins, diagnostic of intense ribosomal biogenesis in pro-erythroblasts preparing for globin chain synthesis
FTH1 (ferritin heavy chain): Iron storage protein essential for haem synthesis; rank-4 position reflects coordination between iron management and proliferation in early erythroblasts
YBX1, HNRNPA1, EEF1B2: RNA-binding and translation elongation factors indicating translational regulation of globin mRNAs during rapid pro-erythroblast expansion
NME4: Nucleotide metabolism enzyme required for nucleotide precursor supply during DNA synthesis in proliferating pro-erythroblasts
suggested_validation: Co-stain primary bone marrow cells with anti-CD71 (transferrin receptor; pro-erythroblast marker), anti-ribosomal protein antibodies, and ferritin to confirm ribosomal biogenesis and iron uptake capacity are simultaneously elevated in CD71+ pro-erythroblasts relative to later erythroid stages

programme_name: CFU-E ribosomal protein synthesis programme
functional_description: This feature marks the CFU-E stage of erythroid differentiation, characterized by intensive ribosomal biogenesis and translational capacity building. The coordinated upregulation of 40S and 60S ribosomal protein subunits (RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPS2, RPL7A, RPL4, RPL37A, RPLP0), translation elongation factors (EEF1B2), and nucleolar proteins (NPM1) reflects the massive protein synthesis demands of the imminent haemoglobin production phase. This precedes the terminal differentiation stages where protein synthesis activity actually decreases.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPS2, RPL7A, RPL4, RPL37A, RPLP0: coordinate 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit proteins diagnostic of ribosomal biogenesis programme
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor indicating activated translational capacity building
NPM1: nucleolar phosphoprotein essential for ribosome assembly, marks proliferative progenitors preparing for terminal differentiation
STMN1: microtubule dynamics regulator consistent with active cell-cycle progression in CFU-E (53% of top cells)
LDHB: lactate dehydrogenase B suggests glycolytic engagement supporting biosynthetic demands of ribosomal protein synthesis
suggested_validation: Quantify ribosomal protein mRNA and rRNA synthesis rates by metabolic labelling (pulse-chase with 4sU) comparing CFU-E vs later-stage erythroblasts; confirm ribosomal assembly by sucrose gradient ultracentrifugation.

programme_name: Early erythroid mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation
functional_description: This programme represents the early-stage erythroid metabolic shift toward energy-intensive haemoglobin synthesis, characterized by robust mitochondrial electron transport chain assembly and ribosomal protein upregulation. The dominant activation in Pro-Erythroblasts (72%) coupled with coordinated expression of Complex I (ND1, ND5, NDUFS5), Complex III (UQCRH, UQCRQ), and Complex IV (CO2, CO3) subunits indicates preparation for high-capacity aerobic ATP production. Concurrent ribosomal protein enrichment (RPL37A, RPS24, RPS23, RPLP0, RPL7A, RPS17) supports the massive translational burden of globin chain synthesis that defines early erythropoiesis.
key_evidence: MT-CO3, MT-CO2, MT-ND1, MT-ND5: Mitochondrial genome-encoded respiratory chain subunits are diagnostic of energy-demanding early erythroid stage before haem-driven growth arrest
UQCRH, UQCRQ, NDUFS5: Nuclear-encoded electron transport chain assembly factors indicate coordinated mitochondrial biogenesis essential for pre-CFU erythroid energetics
RPL37A, RPS24, RPS23, RPLP0, RPL7A, RPS17: Ribosomal proteins cluster as transcriptional co-activators of globin synthesis, pathognomonic for pro-erythroblast translation capacity
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic nucleophosmin-associated factor protects early erythroblasts during metabolic transition before terminal differentiation reduces mitochondrial content
suggested_validation: Perform oxygen consumption rate (OCR) and ATP production assays on FACS-sorted CD71+ Pro-Erythroblasts vs. CFU-E cells, validating that Complex I-IV component co-expression correlates with maximal oxidative capacity at the pro-erythroblast stage.

programme_name: Mitochondrial OXPHOS in early erythroid progenitors
functional_description: This feature marks early-stage erythroid progenitors (Pro-Erythroblasts and CFU-E) undergoing rapid proliferation with high oxidative phosphorylation capacity. The coordinate upregulation of multiple mitochondrial electron transport chain components (MT-ND1, MT-ND5, MT-ND6, MT-CO2, MT-CO3) indicates cells with substantial mitochondrial biogenesis to support energy demands during early erythroid expansion before haem synthesis becomes dominant.
key_evidence: MT-CO3, MT-CO2, MT-ND1, MT-ND5, MT-ND6: All core respiratory chain subunits—diagnostic of mitochondrial biogenesis state rather than mature erythroid metabolism
ATP5IF1: Mitochondrial ATP synthase regulation indicates metabolic remodeling phase; cells balancing ATP production with transition toward haem-driven metabolism
LRPPRC: PPR-repeat protein essential for mitochondrial mRNA stability and translation—required to sustain respiratory chain assembly during proliferative expansion
CDK6 + Cell-type composition (34.5% Pro-Erythroblasts, 23.5% Megakaryocyte Precursors): G1/S checkpoint control in multipotent progenitors before lineage-specific metabolic commitment
suggested_validation: Sort Pro-Erythroblasts vs. Basophilic Erythroblasts, perform quantitative proteomics on respiratory chain complexes I-IV, and measure mitochondrial membrane potential (JC-1 staining) to confirm OXPHOS capacity declines with erythroid maturation.

programme_name: Early erythroid translational capacity expansion
functional_description: Pro-erythroblasts and early CFU-E cells activate a coordinated programme of ribosomal protein synthesis and mitochondrial bioenergetics to support the massive protein synthetic demands of haemoglobin accumulation. This combines elevated ribosomal subunit assembly (RPS/RPL genes), translation elongation factors (EEF1B2), and oxidative phosphorylation capacity (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1) to fuel rapid proliferation and globin chain synthesis during early erythroid commitment.
key_evidence: RPLP0, RPS2, RPL4, RPS17, RPS23, RPS24, RPL37A, RPL7A: Coordinately upregulated ribosomal proteins diagnostic of translational machinery scaling in high-biosynthetic-demand stages
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor required for sustained polypeptide chain elongation during globin synthesis ramp-up
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1: Mitochondrial electron transport chain components indicating increased ATP generation to power protein synthesis and nucleotide biosynthesis
YBX1, HNRNPA1: RNA-binding proteins involved in translational control and mRNA stabilisation of globin chains
suggested_validation: Quantify translation rate via puromycin incorporation or [35S]methionine pulse-chase in FACS-sorted pro-erythroblasts vs CFU-E vs mature erythroblasts; correlate with ribosomal occupancy via polysome profiling on sorted populations

programme_name: Early erythroid ribosome biogenesis and translational capacity
functional_description: This programme represents the intensive ribosomal protein synthesis and translational machinery assembly occurring in CFU-E and pro-erythroblasts during early erythroid commitment. The coordinated upregulation of >8 ribosomal proteins (RPS2, RPS17, RPS23, RPS24, RPL4, RPL7A, RPL37A, RPLP0) and translation factors (EEF1B2) reflects the massive protein synthetic demand required for haemoglobin accumulation. Concurrent upregulation of nucleotide metabolism (IMPDH2), mitochondrial function (UQCRH), and nucleolar organization (NPM1, HMGN1) supports the biosynthetic and energetic requirements of this highly proliferative differentiation stage.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS17, RPS2, RPS23, RPL4, RPL7A, RPL37A, RPLP0: Eight distinct ribosomal structural proteins collectively indicating global ribosome biogenesis—diagnostic of translational upregulation in early erythroid progenitors
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor indicates heightened protein synthesis elongation capacity required for rapid haemoglobin chain synthesis
IMPDH2: Rate-limiting guanine nucleotide biosynthesis enzyme essential for ribosomal RNA and mRNA synthesis during ribosome assembly in proliferating progenitors
NPM1, HMGN1: Nucleolar proteins involved in ribosomal assembly and ribosomal RNA processing, marking active nucleolar function in this stage
UQCRH: Mitochondrial complex III component supporting oxidative ATP production required for energy-intensive protein synthesis
suggested_validation: Perform polysome profiling (sucrose gradient ultracentrifugation) on sorted CFU-E and pro-erythroblasts versus later-stage erythroblasts to confirm elevated polysome abundance and translational activity in feature-positive cells

programme_name: Proliferating erythroid progenitor translational machinery
functional_description: This feature captures the hyperactivation of ribosomal biogenesis and protein synthesis machinery in actively cycling erythroid progenitors (CFU-E, Pro-Erythroblasts). The coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4), translation elongation factors (EEF1B2), and metabolic enzymes (GAPDH, LDHB, UQCRH) reflects the massive protein production demand during rapid haemoglobin synthesis and cellular proliferation in early-stage erythropoiesis.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4: Core ribosomal protein subunits diagnostic of active ribosome biogenesis during proliferation
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor required for rapid protein synthesis in dividing cells
GAPDH, LDHB, UQCRH: Glycolytic and OXPHOS enzymes supporting the bioenergetic demands of proliferation and haemoglobin synthesis
Cell composition: 32.5% CFU-E (colony-forming erythroid) + 17.5% Pro-Erythroblasts confirms early proliferative erythroid stages
suggested_validation: Fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH) or immunofluorescence co-staining of CD71 (transferrin receptor) with RPL37A or RPS24 to confirm feature activation in cycling erythroid progenitors versus non-cycling late-stage erythroblasts

programme_name: Early erythroid ribosomal translation and iron metabolism
functional_description: This programme represents the translational machinery activation coupled with iron homeostasis in pro-erythroblasts and basophilic erythroblasts. The coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (RPL4, RPLP0, RPS2/17/23/24, RPL7A, RPL37A), translation factors (EEF1B2), and iron storage protein FTH1 reflects the massive synthetic capacity required for haemoglobin production while managing the iron influx needed for haem synthesis. YBX1 acts as a translational regulator of iron-responsive transcripts, while mitochondrial oxidoreductases (MT-CO2/3) support the energetic demands of ribosome biogenesis and protein synthesis.
key_evidence: FTH1: Essential iron storage during peak haemoglobin synthesis; ironically required to prevent iron-induced apoptosis in erythroid progenitors
RPL4/RPLP0/RPS2/RPS17/RPS23/RPS24/RPL7A/RPL37A: Eight ribosomal proteins indicate wholesale translational apparatus upregulation diagnostic of rapid protein synthesis phase
YBX1: Cold shock domain protein regulating translation of iron metabolism genes (IRPs); critical for coordinating globin synthesis with iron availability
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor indicating active protein elongation cycle, not initiation bottleneck
MT-CO2/MT-CO3: Mitochondrial electron transport proteins supporting ATP production for protein synthesis and haem biosynthesis in early erythroids
suggested_validation: Co-immunoprecipitation of YBX1 with transferrin receptor mRNA (TFRC) in sorted pro-erythroblasts vs. basophilic erythroblasts to validate translational coordination of iron uptake machinery with ribosomal activation.

programme_name: Early erythroid mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation
functional_description: This programme represents the early pro-erythroblast stage characterized by active mitochondrial bioenergetics to support the massive ATP demands of rapid proliferation and haemoglobin synthesis. The coordinated upregulation of multi-subunit OXPHOS complexes (Complex I: MT-ND1, MT-ND5, NDUFS5, NDUFB9; Complex III: UQCRQ; Complex IV: MT-CO2, MT-CO3) indicates maximal oxidative ATP generation before the metabolic transition to glycolysis-dominance in later erythroid stages. Supporting factors include ribosomal machinery (RPL37A) for high-rate protein synthesis and nuclear protective proteins (HMGB1, BANF1, PTMA) stabilizing the pro-erythroblast nuclei during active transcription.
key_evidence: MT-CO3, MT-CO2, MT-ND1, MT-ND5: Core electron transport chain subunits diagnostic of active OXPHOS in energy-demanding pro-erythroblasts
UQCRQ, NDUFS5, NDUFB9: Accessory OXPHOS components confirming coordinated multi-complex biogenesis rather than single-complex upregulation
59.5% Pro-Erythroblast enrichment: Validates stage-specificity to earliest erythroid progenitor with highest mitochondrial density
RPL37A: Reflects intense ribosomal demand for haemoglobin synthesis during proliferative pro-erythroblast phase
suggested_validation: Quantify mitochondrial membrane potential (TMRM or JC-1 staining) and oxygen consumption rate (Seahorse) comparing isolated pro-erythroblasts vs later CFU-E and basophilic erythroblasts to confirm OXPHOS activity decreases with differentiation.

programme_name: MHC-II antigen presentation in B-cell and pDC
functional_description: This feature marks professional antigen-presenting cells (B cells and pDCs) characterized by coordinated expression of HLA class II molecules (HLA-DRA, HLA-DQB1, HLA-DMA/B) and the chaperone CD74 required for peptide loading. The co-expression of B-cell identity genes (CD79A, TCF4, SOX4, AFF3) and pDC-specific factors (IRF4, SPIB) alongside MHC-II machinery defines cells committed to antigen presentation across both lineages.
key_evidence: CD74: Essential chaperone for MHC-II peptide loading; diagnostic of antigen-presenting cell state
HLA-DRA/DQB1/DMA/DMB: Complete HLA class II presentation module upregulated coordinately; enables exogenous antigen processing
TCF4 + SOX4 + AFF3: Transcriptional regulators driving B-cell and pDC differentiation; TCF4 is master regulator of pDC development
IRF4 + SPIB: Interferon regulatory factors controlling both B-cell and pDC terminal differentiation; IRF4 required for pDC TLR response
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of HLA-DR surface expression with CD79A (B cells) and CD303/BDCA-2 (pDCs) on SAE feature-high vs feature-low cells to validate MHC-II+ antigen-presenting cell identity

programme_name: MHC-II antigen presentation maturation cDC1
functional_description: This feature captures the transcriptional programme of classical dendritic cell (cDC1) maturation characterized by coordinated upregulation of the complete MHC-II presentation machinery (HLA-DR, HLA-DQ, HLA-DP heterodimers and CD74 chaperone). The dominance of cDC1 (62%) with Pre-cDC (19.5%) suggests this represents the functional maturation checkpoint where cDCs acquire full antigen presentation capacity, supported by cathepsin-associated antigen processing genes (CPVL) and myeloid differentiation drivers (SPI1).
key_evidence: CD74: MHC-II-associated invariant chain essential for HLA-II assembly and trafficking—diagnostic marker of functional antigen-presenting cells
HLA-DRA/DRB1, HLA-DQA1/DQB1, HLA-DPA1/DPB1: Complete HLA class II heterodimer set indicates mature, competent antigen presentation phenotype
HLA-DMA/DMB: Peptide exchange catalysts required for high-affinity MHC-II binding—signature of activated professional APCs
SPI1: PU.1 transcription factor drives myeloid/APC differentiation and MHC-II locus accessibility
CPVL: Carboxypeptidase enables precise antigen processing for optimal MHC-II presentation
suggested_validation: FACS sort CD74+HLA-DR++ cells from bone marrow Pre-cDC and cDC1 populations, perform MHC-II peptide-binding assay and in vitro T-cell activation assay to confirm functional maturation of antigen presentation capacity

programme_name: HLA class II antigen presentation in dendritic cells
functional_description: This feature captures the core MHC class II antigen presentation machinery specifically upregulated in mature dendritic cells (cDC1 and cDC2). The programme is characterized by coordinated expression of HLA class II α and β chain components (HLA-DR, HLA-DQ, HLA-DP) and the invariant chain CD74, which is essential for proper MHC-II trafficking, peptide loading via HLA-DM, and immunological synapse formation. This represents the professional antigen-presenting cell state optimized for T cell activation.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA/HLA-DRB1: Core HLA-DR heterodimer - dominant MHC-II molecule on dendritic cells for CD4+ T cell presentation
HLA-DPA1/HLA-DPB1 & HLA-DQA1/HLA-DQB1: Complementary HLA-DP and HLA-DQ class II molecules expanding peptide presentation capacity
CD74: Invariant chain required for MHC-II assembly, trafficking, and initial peptide loading; diagnostic marker of professional APCs
HLA-DMA/HLA-DMB: Non-classical MHC-II molecules mediating peptide exchange in endosomal compartments - essential for optimal antigen presentation
FCGRT: IgG Fc receptor supporting antibody-mediated antigen uptake and cross-presentation capacity of dendritic cells
SPI1: PU.1 transcription factor driving myeloid differentiation and directly activates HLA and antigen presentation genes
suggested_validation: ATAC-seq or ChIP-seq for CIITA/RFX5 binding at HLA and CD74 loci to confirm coordinated class II transcriptional regulation; validate by flow cytometry for HLA-DR/DQ/DP surface expression intensity in cDC1 vs cDC2 subsets

programme_name: Classical monocyte maturation and antimicrobial activation
functional_description: This programme defines the classical monocyte (CD14+) lineage with robust upregulation of S100 calcium-binding proteins (S100A8/A9 heterodimer) that drive innate immune responses and bactericidal activity. The co-expression of lysozyme (LYZ), ficolin-1 (FCN1), and cystatin-A (CSTA) indicates maturation towards a pro-inflammatory, antimicrobial effector state characteristic of circulating CD14+ monocytes engaged in pathogen sensing and phagocytosis.
key_evidence: S100A8/A9: Calprotectin heterodimer; canonical markers of classical monocytes with antimicrobial and inflammatory signalling capacity
LYZ: Lysozyme secretion defining monocyte bactericidal function; diagnostic of mature myeloid differentiation
FCN1: Ficolin-1 (M-ficolin); pattern recognition receptor upregulated in activated classical monocytes for complement-independent pathogen recognition
TYROBP (DAP12): Immunoreceptor signalling adapter; couples phagocytic receptors to downstream activation in innate immunity
MNDA: Myeloid nuclear differentiation antigen; myeloid-restricted marker confirming monocytic lineage identity
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of CD14+ monocytes with S100A9, LYZ, and FCN1 to confirm co-expression in classical monocyte subset and compare expression across monocyte subsets (intermediate, non-classical).

programme_name: CD16+ non-classical monocyte iron-lysosomal metabolic state
functional_description: This programme identifies CD16+ non-classical monocytes in an iron-laden, lysosomal-active metabolic state. The dominant expression of FTH1 (ferritin heavy chain) coupled with lysosomal cathepsins (CTSS) and cysteine proteases indicates cells actively managing intracellular iron metabolism and sustaining lysosomal degradative capacity. Co-expression of FCGR3A (CD16 receptor) confirms non-classical monocyte identity, while S100 family proteins and TYROBP suggest enhanced inflammatory responsiveness and actin dynamics.
key_evidence: FTH1: Rate-limiting iron storage in iron-recycling non-classical monocytes with high erythrophagocytic/haem turnover capacity
FCGR3A: Defines CD16+ non-classical monocyte identity with enhanced Fc-receptor mediated immune recognition
CTSS + CST3: Lysosomal cysteine proteases and cystatins indicate active lysosomal degradation pathway for haem/iron processing
TYROBP: ITAM-signalling adapter essential for non-classical monocyte inflammatory activation
S100A4/A11: Calcium-responsive inflammatory mediators characteristic of tissue-patrolling non-classical monocytes
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry sorting of CD14-CD16+ monocytes followed by iron staining (Perls' Prussian blue or ferritin immunofluorescence) combined with scRNA-seq to confirm FTH1/CTSS co-expression validates iron-handling lysosomal state in non-classical monocytes.

programme_name: Iron metabolism and stress response in myeloid cells
functional_description: This programme represents metabolically active myeloid cells (CD16 monocytes and cDC2) engaged in iron homeostasis and oxidative stress management. The dominant expression of FTH1 (ferritin heavy chain), SAT1 (polyamine catabolism), and NAMPT (NAD+ salvage pathway) indicates cells handling high iron loads and managing reactive oxygen species through antioxidant and energetic pathways. The admixture of early erythroid progenitors (CFU-E, Pro-Erythroblasts) likely reflects shared iron-dependent metabolic stress responses during haem synthesis.
key_evidence: FTH1 (rank 1): Ferritin heavy chain diagnostic for iron storage capacity; monocytes and erythroid progenitors both manage high intracellular iron
SAT1 (rank 2): Rate-limiting polyamine catabolism enzyme; generates acetyl-CoA and maintains redox balance under oxidative stress
NAMPT (rank 4): NAD+ biosynthesis enzyme; critical for metabolic resilience and stress tolerance in metabolically active immune cells
SPI1 (rank 9): PU.1 transcription factor; master regulator of myeloid differentiation and iron metabolism programmes
TYROBP (rank 8): DAP12 adaptor; mediates activation signals in monocytes/dendritic cells consistent with primary cell-type composition
suggested_validation: Co-stain top 200 activating cells with PERLS iron stain and intracellular ROS detection (DHE/DCFDA) to confirm elevated iron uptake and oxidative stress in CD16 monocytes/cDC2, distinguishing metabolic stress response from classical antigen presentation programme

programme_name: Classical monocyte myeloid maturation and inflammation
functional_description: This feature captures the late-stage classical monocyte differentiation programme characterized by elevated S100 calcium-binding proteins (S100A8/A9/A6/A12/A4) that drive innate immune responses and myeloid cell activation. The co-expression of myeloid differentiation markers (MNDA, TYROBP, AIF1) alongside ficolin-1 (FCN1) and granulin (GRN) indicates mature classical monocytes poised for pathogen recognition and inflammatory responses. The minor megakaryocyte precursor contamination (25%) likely reflects shared myeloid progenitor transcriptional states rather than true differentiation overlap.
key_evidence: S100A8/A9: Canonical calprotectin heterodimer; hallmark of classical monocytes and active myeloid inflammation
FCN1: Ficolins are complement-like pattern recognition receptors enriched in CD14+ monocytes for innate immunity
MNDA: Myeloid-restricted nuclear marker exclusively in granulocytes/monocytes, diagnostic of myeloid maturation
TYROBP: DAP12 adaptor required for ITAM signaling in mature monocyte inflammatory function
GRN: Secreted granulins involved in monocyte-mediated tissue inflammation and remodeling
suggested_validation: FACS sort CD14+S100A8+ classical monocytes and perform RNA-seq to confirm this feature specifically activates in mature classical monocytes; validate S100A8/A9 protein expression by flow cytometry on the top 200 cells

programme_name: Early erythroid proliferation with iron metabolism
functional_description: This feature marks the transition from pro-erythroblasts to basophilic erythroblasts, characterized by active ribosomal biogenesis (RPL4, RPL37A, RPLP0, HNRNPF, RANBP1, PA2G4, NOP10) supporting rapid protein synthesis during proliferation. Concurrent upregulation of iron storage (FTH1) and stress response proteins (HMGB1, YBX1, S100A6) reflects the metabolic demands of early haem synthesis and iron trafficking that precede haemoglobin accumulation.
key_evidence: FTH1: Iron storage enzyme essential for managing iron influx during early haem biosynthesis in basophilic erythroblasts
RPL4, RPL37A, RPLP0: Ribosomal proteins diagnostic of active translation machinery during proliferative expansion
NOP10, PA2G4: snoRNP components directing ribosomal RNA modification, rate-limiting for ribosome biogenesis in proliferating cells
YBX1, HMGB1: RNA-binding proteins managing nucleotide stress and stabilizing mRNAs encoding haem biosynthetic enzymes
ATP5IF1: Mitochondrial ATP regulation reflecting high ATP demand of ribosomal assembly and iron transport
suggested_validation: Sort pro-erythroblasts and basophilic erythroblasts by FTH1+RPL4+ co-expression and validate increased haem synthase activity (ALAS2, FECH) and 55S ribosomal particle abundance by flow cytometry and electron microscopy

programme_name: Proliferative erythro-megakaryocytic progenitor metabolism
functional_description: This feature marks actively proliferating early erythroid and megakaryocytic progenitors characterized by elevated protein synthesis capacity (ribosomal proteins RPS24, RPS17, RPLP0), mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (NDUFB9, MT-CO3, SOD1), and nucleotide metabolism (ERH). The enrichment of RNA-binding proteins (YBX1, HMGB1, PTMA) and chaperones (PPIA) reflects the high biosynthetic demand of actively dividing progenitors rather than quiescent HSCs or terminally differentiated cells.
key_evidence: YBX1: RNA-binding protein essential for translational control during rapid cell division in early progenitors
NDUFB9 + MT-CO3 + SOD1: Mitochondrial OXPHOS and ROS management signature of metabolically active proliferating cells
RPS24 + RPS17 + RPLP0: Ribosomal proteins reflecting heightened translation capacity in G1/S phase progenitors
PTMA + HMGB1: Nuclear protein abundance in proliferating cells; PTMA provides apoptosis resistance during expansion
SLC25A3 + RANBP1: Phosphate transport and nucleotide biosynthesis supporting DNA replication in S-phase cells
suggested_validation: Sort CD34+ pro-erythroblasts and megakaryocyte precursors by Ki-67 expression; confirm elevated YBX1, ribosomal protein, and OXPHOS gene expression in the Ki-67+ proliferative fraction by RT-qPCR or proteomics.

programme_name: B-cell cycling with nucleosomal dynamics
functional_description: This programme reflects active cell cycle progression in early B-cell progenitors (Large Pre-B and Pro-B Cycling dominance), characterized by elevated tubulin/cytoskeletal proteins (TUBA1B, TUBB) for mitotic spindle assembly, chromatin remodeling factors (HMGN2, HMGB1/2, H2AFZ), and nucleoprotein chaperones (PTMA, PPIA) enabling rapid DNA replication and transcription. The enrichment of splicing factors (HNRNPA1/2B1/A3, SRSF3) and ribosomal proteins (RPS24) supports coordinated RNA processing during S/G2 phase when protein synthesis demands are high.
key_evidence: STMN1: Stathmin regulates microtubule dynamics during mitosis; diagnostic of active cycling
TUBA1B + TUBB: Spindle apparatus components essential for mitotic progression in rapidly dividing progenitors
HMGN2 + HMGB1/2: Nucleosomal architecture remodelers enabling accessible chromatin for DNA replication and transcription
PTMA: Nucleoprotein chaperon protecting DNA/histones during replication stress; marks S-phase cells
HNRNPA1/A2B1/A3 + SRSF3: Pre-mRNA processing upregulation coupled to cell cycle checkpoints in proliferating cells
suggested_validation: Co-stain sorted Large Pre-B/Pro-B cycling cells with Ki-67 (proliferation) and EdU (S-phase incorporation) versus phospho-histone H3 (M-phase), confirming Feature 58 activators are predominantly in S/G2 phases of the cell cycle.

programme_name: Early erythroid ribosome biogenesis and RNA processing
functional_description: This programme represents the intense ribosomal protein synthesis and rRNA processing activity required during pro-erythroblast and basophilic erythroblast expansion. The coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (RPLP0, RPL37A, RPS2), snoRNP components (NOP10), RNA-binding proteins (YBX1, PA2G4), and splicing factors (SRSF3, SNRPE) reflects the massive translational capacity needed to synthesize haemoglobin and other proteins during rapid erythroid proliferation.
key_evidence: NOP10: H/ACA snoRNP component diagnostic of active rRNA pseudouridylation during ribosome biogenesis
RPLP0, RPL37A, RPS2: Ribosomal structural proteins required for 40S and 60S assembly in proliferating erythroid cells
YBX1, PA2G4: RNA-binding proteins functioning in pre-ribosomal particle assembly and nucleolar trafficking
SLBP: Histone mRNA stem-loop binding factor reflecting S-phase active replication machinery in basophilic erythroblasts
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain supporting iron storage during intensive haemoglobin synthesis
HMGB1: Nucleoid-associated protein facilitating chromatin remodelling and ribosomal gene transcription
suggested_validation: Perform nucleolar isolation followed by qPCR quantification of 18S/28S rRNA synthesis and snoRNP occupancy in FACS-sorted pro-erythroblasts vs. polychromatic erythroblasts to confirm ribosome biogenesis activity peaks at the basophilic stage

programme_name: Megakaryocyte-dendritic metabolic priming via oxidative phosphorylation
functional_description: This programme reflects metabolic preparation in megakaryocyte precursors and cDC lineage cells through coordinated upregulation of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (COX5A, VDAC1, SLC25A5), glycolytic capacity (ENO1, LDHA), and detoxification systems (GSTP1). The co-expression of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS23) with autophagy machinery (ATG3) and energy metabolism enzymes suggests preparation for both biosynthetic demands and stress resilience characteristic of these cell types during differentiation.
key_evidence: COX5A & VDAC1: Terminal oxidative phosphorylation and mitochondrial ATP/metabolite transport—diagnostic of energy-demanding differentiation stages in megakaryocytes and antigen-presenting dendritic cells
ENO1 & LDHA: Glycolytic priming for rapid ATP generation and lactate-mediated signalling in proliferative/migratory dendritic cells and polyploidizing megakaryocytes
GSTP1: Antioxidant defence via glutathione conjugation—essential for handling ROS from high mitochondrial activity during megakaryopoiesis and DC maturation
ATG3 & PTMA: Autophagy and apoptosis regulation suggesting metabolic stress adaptation and selective survival during lineage commitment
suggested_validation: Measure real-time oxygen consumption rate (OCR) and extracellular acidification rate (ECAR) in flow-sorted megakaryocyte precursors vs cDC1 vs pre-cDC to quantify OXPHOS/glycolytic dependency and confirm metabolic priming state.

programme_name: Megakaryocyte precursor proliferative metabolic priming
functional_description: This programme characterizes proliferating megakaryocyte precursors undergoing rapid cell division and polyploidization, marked by enhanced glycolytic metabolism (GAPDH, ENO1), mitochondrial bioenergetics (VDAC1, SLC25A5), and RNA processing capacity (SRSF3, HNRNPC, HNRNPA2B1). Co-expression of anti-apoptotic factors (PTMA) with signal transduction adaptors (YWHAQ/YWHAE) and DNA-binding proteins (HMGN2, DEK) reflects the metabolic and transcriptional remodelling required to support the extraordinary biosynthetic demands of megakaryocytic polyploidization.
key_evidence: GAPDH + ENO1: Glycolytic enzymes diagnostic of high metabolic flux in proliferating megakaryocyte precursors
VDAC1 + SLC25A5: Mitochondrial outer membrane transporters supporting increased energy demands during megakaryocyte expansion
SRSF3 + HNRNPC + HNRNPA2B1: SR proteins and hnRNPs required for pre-mRNA splicing during rapid proliferation and lineage-specific transcript isoform switching
YWHAQ + YWHAE: 14-3-3 signalling adaptors supporting survival signalling in proliferating precursors
PTMA + HMGN2 + DEK: Nuclear factors promoting transcriptional activity and chromatin remodelling during polyploidization
suggested_validation: Co-stain CD41+CD34+ megakaryocyte precursors with Ki-67 and TMRE (mitochondrial membrane potential) to confirm proliferation and metabolic activity correlates with feature activation; validate RNA splicing factor enrichment by RNA-seq of feature+ versus feature- megakaryocyte precursors.

programme_name: Small Pre-B cell development with metabolic priming
functional_description: This feature marks Small Pre-B cells (35.5% of top 200) undergoing late pre-BCR checkpoints with concurrent metabolic reprogramming toward acetyl-CoA synthesis and fatty acid metabolism. The co-expression of B-cell identity genes (CD79B, BCL7A, VPREB3, TCL1A) with mitochondrial energetic modulators (ACSS1, ATP5IF1, ACSM3) and DNA repair machinery (NEIL1, REXO2) indicates cells actively resolving V(D)J recombination while preparing for proliferative expansion.
key_evidence: CD79B: B-cell receptor complex component, diagnostic for B-lineage commitment and pre-BCR signalling
VPREB3: Pre-B cell receptor surrogate light chain, exclusively expressed during small pre-B stage
TCL1A: Co-expressed with pre-BCR, promotes pre-B cell survival and proliferation
ACSS1 + ACSM3: Mitochondrial acetyl-CoA synthesis enzymes indicating metabolic shift to support proliferation
NEIL1 + REXO2: DNA repair and processing enzymes active during V(D)J recombination completion
ATP5IF1: Mitochondrial ATP synthase inhibitor suggesting metabolic remodelling during transition to large pre-B
suggested_validation: Co-stain flow cytometry for CD19+ CD34- CD10+ (small pre-B) with MitoTracker and ACSS1/ACSL1 intracellular staining to confirm metabolic priming at pre-BCR checkpoint

programme_name: Proliferation-associated proteasomal catabolism
functional_description: This feature defines a proliferative programme characterized by elevated proteasomal degradation (PSMA4, PSMA5), cytoskeletal remodelling (ACTG1, TMSB4X, STMN1), and glycolytic metabolism (LDHA) supporting rapid cell division. The programme is driven by a mixed composition of T cell and megakaryocyte precursor lineages, both requiring heightened anabolic/catabolic flux during proliferation. Co-expression of splicing factors (SNRPG, HNRNPA2B1, LSM5) and mitotic machinery (SKA2) indicates active remodelling of both protein and RNA processing to sustain high proliferation rates.
key_evidence: PSMA4 & PSMA5: Core 20S proteasome subunits diagnostic of elevated protein degradation during proliferation
STMN1: Microtubule dynamics regulator essential for mitotic spindle assembly and cytokinesis
LDHA: Glycolytic enzyme supporting energetically demanding cell division under rapid growth
ACTG1 & TMSB4X: Actin regulation enabling cytoskeletal reorganisation during cell cycle progression
SKA2: Spindle assembly checkpoint component required for accurate chromosome segregation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining for Ki67/PCNA with PSMA4/PSMA5 protein levels across sorted T cell and megakaryocyte precursor populations to confirm proteasome upregulation correlates with S/G2M phase enrichment

programme_name: G2/M mitotic checkpoint and spindle assembly
functional_description: This programme represents cells in active G2/M phase with coordinated expression of mitotic machinery, microtubule dynamics, and DNA topology management. The dominant cell-type composition (41.5% Large Pre-B cells with secondary cycling progenitors and megakaryocyte precursors) indicates this is a proliferation-stage-agnostic programme active across multiple lymphoid and erythroid lineages undergoing rapid divisions.
key_evidence: STMN1: Stathmin regulates microtubule dynamics and is a canonical G2/M marker; essential for mitotic spindle assembly
AURKB: Aurora kinase B is a core mitotic checkpoint kinase required for cytokinesis and chromosome segregation
TOP2A: DNA topoisomerase II is essential for decatenation of sister chromatids during mitosis; activity peaks in S/G2/M phases
NUSAP1: Spindle-associated protein directly involved in microtubule organization during mitosis
TUBB + TUBA1B: Tubulin heterodimers are structural components of mitotic spindles; co-expression indicates active microtubule assembly
HMGB1/HMGB2/HMGN2: High mobility group proteins facilitate chromatin remodelling during mitotic progression and are upregulated in cycling cells
suggested_validation: Live-cell imaging with Hoechst/DAPI staining combined with immunofluorescence for phospho-histone H3 (pHH3) and Aurora B to confirm feature-positive cells are specifically enriched in G2/M phase across the multi-lineage composition

programme_name: Erythroid S-phase chromatin remodeling and ribosome biogenesis
functional_description: This programme represents proliferating erythroid progenitors (polychromatic and pro-erythroblasts) in active DNA synthesis phase, characterized by upregulation of chromatin remodeling factors (HMGN2, HMGB2, DEK, H3F3A, H2AFZ, H2AFY) that facilitate transcriptional access during rapid proliferation, coupled with ribosomal protein synthesis (RPS24, TUBA1B, TUBB) and nucleotide metabolism (TALDO1 via pentose phosphate pathway) supporting mass production of haemoglobin and cellular machinery.
key_evidence: HMGN2, HMGB2, DEK, H3F3A: Core nucleosome-binding and chromatin remodeling proteins diagnostic of active transcription during S-phase proliferation
H2AFZ, H2AFY: Histone variants enriched at active promoters, essential for maintaining open chromatin during rapid erythroid proliferation
CKS1B, TUBA1B, TUBB: Cell cycle checkpoint and cytoskeletal proteins marking active G1/S transition and cytokinesis in cycling erythroblasts
TALDO1: Pentose phosphate pathway enzyme generating ribose-5-phosphate for nucleotide biosynthesis, critical metabolic demand of erythroid proliferation
RPS24, ribosomal biogenesis genes: Supporting elevated protein synthesis required for haemoglobin production in proliferating erythroblasts
suggested_validation: FACS-sort polychromatic erythroblasts by BrdU/EdU incorporation (S-phase) vs G0/G1 and perform qRT-PCR/Western blot comparing chromatin remodeling (HMGN2, HMGB2) and PPP enzyme (TALDO1) expression across cell cycle phases

programme_name: Early erythroid progenitor with B-cell contamination
functional_description: This feature marks early-stage erythroid progenitors (Pro-Erythroblasts/Basophilic Erythroblasts) with significant B-cell lineage contamination. The erythroid signal is driven by iron metabolism genes (TFR2, GLRX5) and erythropoietin signalling (EPOR), while B-cell identity genes (CD79B, BCL7A) and mitochondrial metabolic genes (ATP5IF1, ACSM3) reflect B-lymphoid co-activation, suggesting either a mixed population artifact or genuine cross-lineage priming at the haematopoietic progenitor level.
key_evidence: EPOR: Canonical early erythroid lineage specification via erythropoietin receptor signalling
TFR2: Transferrin receptor essential for iron uptake during haem synthesis in erythroid maturation
CD79B: B-cell receptor complex component diagnostic of B-lymphoid lineage identity (20.5% Small Pre-B cells)
GLRX5: Mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis required for early erythroid haem biosynthesis
ATP5IF1: ATP synthase inhibition marker of metabolic quiescence in early progenitors
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of top 200 cells for CD34/CD71/EPOR (erythroid) vs CD79B/CD19 (B-cell) to quantify lineage purity; if >50% are genuinely CD34+CD71+ with CD79B co-expression, this reflects a multipotent progenitor state rather than contamination.

programme_name: Stromal niche cytokine and complement regulation
functional_description: This programme represents bone marrow stromal cells engaged in haematopoietic niche signalling through chemokine secretion (CXCL12), complement/coagulation cascade regulation (SERPING1, TFPI, CFD), and secretion of growth factors (GAS6, MDK) that support megakaryocyte development. The minor megakaryocyte contamination (27.5%) likely reflects physical proximity and paracrine signalling interactions rather than intrinsic megakaryocyte function.
key_evidence: CXCL12: Canonical stromal niche cytokine essential for HSC retention and megakaryocyte positioning in bone marrow microenvironment
SERPING1: Complement C1-esterase inhibitor secreted by stromal cells to regulate inflammation and support haematopoietic cell survival
LEPR: Leptin receptor on stromal cells involved in niche function and megakaryopoiesis support
GAS6: Secreted growth factor promoting megakaryocyte maturation and platelet production
TFPI: Anticoagulant protease inhibitor produced by stromal cells to maintain local haemostatic balance
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry sort of CD45-negative stromal cells and validate CXCL12, GAS6, and SERPING1 protein expression; co-culture assay with CD34+ cells or megakaryocyte progenitors to confirm functional paracrine support.

programme_name: Large Pre-B cell translational capacity burst
functional_description: This programme captures a translational amplification state in large pre-B cells characterized by coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (40S and 60S subunits), translation elongation factors, and glycolytic enzymes. This reflects the energetic and biosynthetic demands of large pre-B cells undergoing rapid protein synthesis during the pre-BCR signalling checkpoint, likely supporting the expansion phase after successful VDJ recombination.
key_evidence: RPS17, RPS2, RPL7A, RPL37A, RPL4, RPS24, RPS23: comprehensive ribosomal protein signature (both 40S and 60S components) indicating global translational machinery upscaling
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor diagnostic of active translation rate acceleration
GAPDH, ENO1: glycolytic enzymes supporting ATP/NADH requirements for high-rate protein synthesis
HNRNPA1, HMGN1: RNA processing and chromatin accessibility factors supporting transcriptional-translational coupling in proliferative cells
suggested_validation: Ribosome profiling (Ribo-seq) on sorted large pre-B cells vs. small pre-B or pro-B cells to quantify polysome abundance and translation rates genome-wide

programme_name: Megakaryocyte precursor proliferation chromatin remodelling
functional_description: This programme represents actively proliferating megakaryocyte precursors characterized by open chromatin architecture (HMGN2, HMGB1, DEK, H2AFY nucleosome remodelling), elevated glycolytic metabolism (ENO1, GAPDH, LDHA) supporting cell division, and coordinated RNA processing machinery (HNRNPA2B1, SRSF3, LSM5) for rapid transcript synthesis. The co-enrichment of pre-cDC and T cell blasts suggests this captures a general progenitor proliferation programme shared across myeloid and lymphoid compartments during active cell cycle.
key_evidence: HMGN2: Chromatin architecture protein diagnostic of transcriptionally active, proliferating progenitors
ENO1/GAPDH/LDHA: Glycolytic enzymes indicating Warburg-type metabolism supporting rapid cell division
HNRNPA2B1/SRSF3/LSM5: Pre-mRNA splicing factors required for processing transcripts during high biosynthetic demand
DEK/HMGB1: DNA-binding proteins that facilitate chromatin accessibility in dividing cells
56.5% megakaryocyte precursor enrichment: Strong lineage specificity within haematopoietic proliferation context
suggested_validation: Co-stain megakaryocyte precursors (CD34+CD41+) with Ki-67 and measure ATAC-seq accessibility at HMGN2/DEK-marked regions to confirm open chromatin signature in proliferating vs quiescent megakaryocyte progenitors

programme_name: Proliferating progenitor nucleocytoplasmic transport programme
functional_description: This feature marks rapidly dividing progenitors (Large Pre-B, Pro-B Cycling, Pro-Erythroblast) with coordinated upregulation of nucleocytoplasmic trafficking machinery (RANBP1, HMGB1, HMGN2), RNA processing (HNRNPA1/A2B1/A3/C), and mitochondrial biogenesis (SLC25A3, SLC25A5). The dominance of Pre-B cells suggests heightened demand for ribosome and protein synthesis infrastructure accompanying rapid cell division during lymphoid specification.
key_evidence: RANBP1: Essential Ran-GTPase interactor for nuclear-cytoplasmic transport, diagnostic of S/G2-phase proliferating cells requiring constant nucleotide and protein import
HMGB1/HMGN2: Chromatin-binding proteins associated with transcriptionally active, accessible chromatin in proliferating progenitors; required for replication-coupled transcription
HNRNPA1/A2B1/A3/C: Multi-member hnRNP family coordinated upregulation indicates intensive mRNA processing burden (splicing, export) typical of anabolic progenitors
SLC25A3/SLC25A5: Mitochondrial phosphate and ADP/ATP transporters supporting ATP-expensive nucleotide synthesis and ribosome biogenesis
PTMA: Prothymosin-α anti-apoptotic factor permitting sustained proliferation in energy-demanding progenitors
suggested_validation: Perform co-immunofluorescence for RANBP1 + Ki67 + CD34 on sorted Pre-B and Pro-Erythroblast populations to confirm feature marks S-phase cells with active nucleocytoplasmic transport.

programme_name: Pro-erythroblast proliferation with ribosomal biogenesis
functional_description: This programme characterizes early erythroid progenitors (pro-erythroblasts and basophilic erythroblasts) engaged in active proliferation coupled with intensive ribosomal protein synthesis and mitochondrial ATP production. The coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (RPL37A, RPLP0, RPL4, RPS24), mitochondrial ATP synthase subunits (ATP5MC1, ATP5IF1), and iron storage (FTH1) reflects the bioenergetic and translational demands of rapid cell division before haemoglobin synthesis dominates in later erythroid stages.
key_evidence: RPL37A, RPLP0, RPL4, RPS24: Multiple ribosomal proteins diagnostic of active protein synthesis machinery required for proliferation
ATP5MC1, ATP5IF1: Mitochondrial ATP synthase components indicating high energy demand during S/G2 phases of cell cycle
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain for iron sequestration, essential in early erythroid progenitors before globin synthesis peak
YBX1, PA2G4: RNA-binding proteins controlling ribosome biogenesis and cell cycle progression in proliferating cells
GADD45GIP1: Cell cycle regulator, consistent with G1/S checkpoint regulation in actively dividing progenitors
suggested_validation: Sort pro-erythroblasts vs basophilic erythroblasts by BrdU incorporation or Ki-67, then validate feature activation correlates with S-phase marker expression (PCNA, MCM2) and ribosomal protein abundance by flow cytometry

programme_name: Polychromatic erythroblast proliferation with proteostasis
functional_description: This programme represents polychromatic/early-intermediate erythroblasts (43.5% of activators) in active cell cycle combined with megakaryocyte precursors, characterized by coordinated upregulation of protein synthesis machinery (EIF2AK1, ribose metabolism via RPIA), proteasomal degradation (RBX1, UBB, RAD23A), and oxidative stress defence (CAT, IDH2). The expression pattern indicates cells balancing rapid haemoglobin synthesis demands with proteostasis mechanisms to manage protein folding stress during erythroid differentiation.
key_evidence: EIF2AK1: Translation initiation regulator essential for coordinating protein synthesis with metabolic stress in rapidly differentiating erythroblasts
RBX1 + RAD23A + UBB: Proteasomal/ubiquitin-proteasome system components indicating active protein quality control during intense haemoglobin synthesis
RPIA: Pentose phosphate pathway enzyme providing ribose-5-phosphate for nucleotide synthesis in proliferating polychromatic erythroblasts
CAT + IDH2: Antioxidant and mitochondrial metabolism genes addressing ROS from accelerated haemoglobinization
YBX1 + ANP32B: RNA-binding proteins regulating stress response gene expression during erythroid proliferation
suggested_validation: Sort top-200 activating cells by flow cytometry (CD71+CD235a+ gating) and perform ribosome profiling or polysome analysis to directly measure translational capacity and proteostasis load in polychromatic erythroblasts versus early/late erythroblasts

programme_name: Ribosomal protein synthesis during megakaryocyte precursor maturation
functional_description: This feature marks a translational amplification programme characterized by coordinated upregulation of ribosomal protein subunits (RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPL37A, RPL4, RPLP0) and translation elongation factors (EEF1B2). The programme is predominantly active in megakaryocyte precursors (49%), which require massive protein synthesis capacity to produce platelet-scale cytoplasmic volumes and pre-load platelet granules with clotting factors. Concurrent oxidative stress management (GSTP1, GPX1) and mitochondrial respiration (MT-CO2, GAPDH) support the bioenergetic demands of this biosynthetic burst.
key_evidence: RPS24/RPS23/RPS17/RPL4/RPL37A/RPLP0: Six ribosomal protein genes dominating top-15 list indicate coordinated ribosome biogenesis, diagnostic of translation-intensive cells
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor essential for efficient ribosome recycling during high-throughput protein synthesis in megakaryocytes
49% megakaryocyte precursor composition: Megakaryocytic lineage has extreme protein synthesis demands (~1000x normal cell volume) for platelet biogenesis, explaining translational burst activation
GSTP1/GPX1: Detoxification and oxidative stress management genes indicate metabolic stress from sustained ribosomal activity and increased mitochondrial respiration
HNRNPA1/HMGN2: RNA processing and chromatin remodelling factors supporting coordinated transcription-translation coupling during megakaryocyte differentiation
suggested_validation: Perform polysome profiling on sorted megakaryocyte precursors vs other HSPCs to quantify actively translating ribosomes; confirm ribosomal protein mRNA enrichment by qPCR on FACS-isolated megakaryocyte precursors

programme_name: Early erythroblast ribosomal biosynthesis and proliferation
functional_description: This programme represents the peak biosynthetic and proliferative activity of pro-erythroblasts and basophilic erythroblasts, characterized by massive upregulation of ribosomal proteins (RPL4, RPLP0, RPS2, RPL37A) and associated translation machinery to support rapid haemoglobin synthesis. Concurrent expression of mitochondrial bioenergetic genes (ATP5IF1, ATP5MC1, NME4) and iron metabolism (FTH1) reflects the intense metabolic demands of early erythroid expansion, while nucleolar assembly factors (NOP10, PA2G4) and chromatin regulators (HMGB1, PCLAF, YBX1) coordinate the simultaneous demands of proliferation and differentiation.
key_evidence: ATP5IF1, ATP5MC1, NME4: Mitochondrial ATP synthesis and energy metabolism—early erythroblasts require exceptional ATP for rapid protein synthesis and cell division

RPL4, RPLP0, RPS2, RPL37A: Ribosomal structural proteins—diagnostic of the translational factory state required for haemoglobin production; peak in basophilic/pro-erythroblast stages before haem availability limits further synthesis
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain—iron storage coordination essential during early erythroid expansion when iron demand is high but differentiation still permits proliferation
NOP10, PA2G4: Nucleolar snoRNP and ribosome assembly factors—indicate active ribosome biogenesis, the bottleneck for proliferating erythroblasts
HMGB1, YBX1, PCLAF: Nuclear/chromatin regulators—support both proliferation checkpoint control and coordinated chromatin remodelling during rapid differentiation
suggested_validation: FACS-sort pro-erythroblasts and basophilic erythroblasts (CD71+CD36+CD45−) versus polychromatic erythroblasts, and quantify ribosomal protein expression by qPCR and polysome profiling to confirm translation initiation rate correlates with feature activation across the erythroid maturation trajectory.

programme_name: Ribosome biogenesis in proliferating erythro-megakaryocytic progenitors
functional_description: This programme represents active ribosome assembly and protein synthesis machinery activation in highly proliferative early erythroid and megakaryocytic progenitors. The dominant ribosomal protein signature (RPS24, RPS17, RPS26, RPL7A, RPL37A, RPL4) combined with translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) and oxidative phosphorylation components (UQCRH, MT-CO2) reflects the bioenergetic demands of rapid cell division and haemoglobin synthesis during the CFU-E to Pro-Erythroblast transition. The inclusion of redox proteins (TXN, PPIA) supports the metabolic stress management required during intense ribosomal RNA and protein production.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS17, RPS26, RPL7A, RPL37A, RPL4: Comprehensive 40S and 60S ribosomal protein components diagnostic of active ribosome biogenesis rather than basal protein synthesis
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor required for efficient mRNA translation during anabolic phases of proliferation
UQCRH + MT-CO2: Mitochondrial electron transport chain components indicating elevated ATP demand for biosynthetic processes in rapidly dividing progenitors
CFU-E + Pro-Erythroblast dominance (40.5% combined): Cell composition confirms activation in the most proliferative stages before terminal differentiation arrests translation
suggested_validation: Quantify ribosomal RNA (18S/28S) and nascent protein synthesis (puromycin incorporation) rates in sorted CFU-E/Pro-Erythroblast cells vs. mature erythroblasts; compare with parallel metabolic tracing (seahorse analysis) to confirm bioenergetic coupling.

programme_name: Large Pre-B cell cycle S/G2 phase progression
functional_description: This programme marks the proliferative phase of large pre-B cells during late G1/S transition and S/G2 phases, characterized by simultaneous upregulation of DNA synthesis machinery (TYMS), microtubule dynamics (TUBA1B, TUBB, STMN1), and chromatin remodelling factors (HMGB1, HMGB2, HMGN2, DEK). The coordinated expression reflects active replication licensing, nuclear protein shuttling via PTMA, and DNA damage checkpoint surveillance necessary for safe progression through S and G2 phases.
key_evidence: TYMS: Essential deoxyribonucleotide biosynthesis enzyme diagnostic for active DNA synthesis in S phase
STMN1: Microtubule-destabilizing protein required for spindle dynamics and G2/M checkpoint control
HMGB1/HMGB2: High-mobility-group proteins facilitate chromatin accessibility during replication and stress responses
TUBA1B/TUBB: Coordinate upregulation of alpha/beta tubulin for centrosome and mitotic spindle assembly
DEK: DNA-binding protein involved in chromatin topology and transcriptional regulation of proliferation genes
PCLAF: PCNA-associated chromatin remodeller essential for replication fork progression and S-phase fidelity
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry with Ki-67/DAPI staining on sorted Large Pre-B cells to confirm S/G2 phase enrichment and validate TYMS/STMN1 protein expression correlation with DNA content

programme_name: Early erythroid iron metabolism and ribosomal biogenesis
functional_description: This feature captures the early erythroid differentiation programme (Pro-Erythroblast to Basophilic Erythroblast), characterized by coordinated upregulation of iron storage (FTH1), mitochondrial ATP synthesis, and ribosomal proteins. The dominance of FTH1 reflects the massive iron uptake required for haem synthesis, while elevated ribosomal components (RPLP0, RPL37A) and ribosomal assembly factors (NOP10, PA2G4) support the extraordinary protein synthetic demand of early erythropoiesis.
key_evidence: FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain is the diagnostic marker for iron metabolism in early erythroid progenitors preparing for massive haemoglobin synthesis
ATP5IF1, ATP5MC1, NME4: Mitochondrial energy metabolism components essential for ATP-dependent haem synthesis and active iron uptake in early erythroblasts
RPLP0, RPL37A, NOP10, PA2G4: Ribosomal proteins and assembly factors required for the high translational rate needed to synthesize >90% protein mass as haemoglobin in early differentiation
YBX1, SRSF3, HNRNPF: RNA-binding proteins regulating mRNA stability and splicing of erythroid-specific transcripts during proliferative early stages
HMGB1, S100A6: Stress-response and calcium-binding proteins supporting rapid cell cycle progression and nuclear chromatin remodelling in early progenitors
suggested_validation: Single-cell proteomics (flow cytometry or CyTOF) measuring FTH1, mitochondrial membrane potential (TMRM), and CD71 (transferrin receptor) correlation across early erythroid developmental stages to validate iron metabolism and energy state coupling

programme_name: Early erythroid proliferation with ribosome biogenesis
functional_description: This programme marks basophilic and pro-erythroblasts engaged in rapid cell division coupled with intensive ribosome assembly. The co-expression of histone mRNA processing factors (SLBP), snoRNP components (NOP10), and mitochondrial translation machinery (MRPS34, ATP5MC1) with iron storage (FTH1) and RNA-binding proteins (YBX1, HNRNPF, PA2G4) reflects the metabolic demands of early erythroid cells synthesising massive quantities of globin protein and haem-binding machinery.
key_evidence: SLBP: diagnostic marker of active histone mRNA processing during S-phase in rapidly dividing erythroblasts
NOP10: snoRNP involvement in rRNA pseudouridylation, essential for ribosome biogenesis in proliferating cells
FTH1: iron storage protein upregulation required for haem synthesis and Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺ buffering in early erythroid differentiation
MRPS34 + ATP5MC1: mitochondrial translation capacity supporting haemoglobin synthesis and oxidative phosphorylation in basophilic erythroblasts
YBX1 + HNRNPF + PA2G4: coordinated RNA-binding protein activity regulating mRNA stability during proliferative phase
suggested_validation: Sort CD71⁺CD235a⁻ basophilic erythroblasts by SLBP/FTH1 co-expression and validate ribosomal RNA synthesis rate and histone mRNA abundance by qPCR/RNA-seq

programme_name: Mitochondrial oxidative metabolism in megakaryocyte progenitors
functional_description: This programme reflects metabolically active megakaryocyte precursors engaged in mitochondrial respiration and protein synthesis. The coordinated upregulation of cytochrome c oxidase (COX5A), VDAC1 (mitochondrial outer membrane channel), phosphate transporter SLC25A3, and ATP/ADP carrier SLC25A5 indicates robust oxidative phosphorylation. Concurrent elevation of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPL4) and translation factors (EEF1B2) supports the anabolic demands of megakaryocyte development, while GSTP1 and PTMA provide antioxidant and anti-apoptotic protection during this energy-intensive differentiation.
key_evidence: COX5A: Terminal electron transport chain enzyme diagnostic of active mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation
VDAC1: Voltage-dependent anion channel essential for ATP/metabolite exchange across outer mitochondrial membrane
SLC25A3 & SLC25A5: Mitochondrial carriers for phosphate and nucleotides, hallmarks of energy-dependent biosynthesis
RPS24, RPS23, RPL4: Multiple ribosomal proteins indicating high translational capacity for megakaryocyte protein demands
GSTP1: Glutathione transferase providing oxidative stress protection during metabolically intense differentiation
ENO1 & LDHA: Glycolytic enzymes supporting aerobic metabolism and lactate shuttle in progenitor cells
suggested_validation: Measure oxygen consumption rate (OCR) and ATP production in flow-sorted megakaryocyte precursors vs other progenitors using Seahorse XF analyzer; correlate with immunofluorescence for COX activity and mitochondrial mass.
