programme_name: Megakaryocytic progenitor proliferation with RNA processing
functional_description: This feature captures actively proliferating megakaryocyte precursors engaged in coordinated ribosome biogenesis and pre-mRNA splicing. The dominant expression of SR-rich splicing factors (SRSF3, SRSF2), hnRNP family members (HNRNPC, HNRNPA1, HNRNPA2B1), ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPLP0), and chromatin-active nucleolar proteins (HMGN2, DEK, HMGB1) reflects the high biosynthetic demand of MK progenitor expansion. Co-expression of PTMA and YWHAQ indicates active cell cycle progression with apoptosis suppression.
key_evidence: SRSF3, SRSF2: SR-rich splicing factors diagnostic of high transcriptional/translational activity in proliferating progenitors
HNRNPA1, HNRNPC, HNRNPA2B1: hnRNP complex components essential for nuclear RNA metabolism during cell cycle
RPS24, RPLP0: Ribosomal structural proteins indicating active protein synthesis capacity for megakaryocyte differentiation
HMGN2, HMGB1, DEK: Nucleolar and chromatin proteins enabling ribosomal RNA synthesis and nucleosome remodeling
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic factor and transcriptional regulator supporting proliferation maintenance
55.5% Megakaryocyte Precursor composition confirms lineage identity
suggested_validation: Co-immunofluorescence of CD41+ megakaryocyte progenitors with SRSF3 and Ki67 to confirm proliferation status; quantify ribosomal biogenesis rate by pulse-chase 35S labeling in sorted MK precursors with high vs. low feature activation

programme_name: Megakaryocyte-erythroid progenitor translational priming
functional_description: This feature marks early multipotent megakaryocyte and erythroid progenitors undergoing active protein synthesis and RNA processing. The coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPLP0) with SR-rich splicing factors (SRSF2, SRSF3) and RNA-binding proteins (YBX1, HNRNPC) indicates cells preparing for the massive translational demands of cytoplasmic maturation. This programme couples active ribosome biogenesis with splicing fidelity—essential for accurate megakaryocyte platelet protein synthesis and erythroid haemoglobin production.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPLP0: Ribosomal structural proteins diagnostic of active ribosome biogenesis in progenitors before rapid cytoplasmic expansion
SRSF2, SRSF3, SNRPB: SR-rich splicing factors enriched during transition from quiescent to proliferative progenitors; essential for generating mature mRNA in differentiation
YBX1, HNRNPC: Cold-shock domain and hnRNP RNA-binding proteins that coordinate global translational control and mRNA stability during progenitor activation
PTMA: DNA-binding factor and apoptosis inhibitor supporting survival during high biosynthetic demand in early progenitors
COX5A: Mitochondrial complex IV component indicating elevated oxidative metabolism required for energetic demands of biogenesis
suggested_validation: Perform translating ribosome affinity purification (TRAP) or polysome profiling on sorted Megakaryocyte Precursors vs Pro-Erythroblasts to confirm enhanced translation of megakaryocyte-lineage proteins (ITGA2B, GP1BA) and erythroid proteins (GYPA, KLF1), with quantitative mass spectrometry of newly synthesized proteins.

programme_name: Early erythroblast ribosome biosynthesis proliferation
functional_description: This programme is active in pro-erythroblasts and basophilic erythroblasts undergoing rapid proliferation and haemoglobin synthesis. The coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (RPLP0, RPS17, RPS23), snRNP core components (SNRPG, SNRPD1, SNRPE), and oxidative phosphorylation machinery (UQCRH, UQCRQ, NDUFS5) reflects the massive translational capacity and ATP demand required for concurrent cell division and globin chain synthesis. The inclusion of PTMA (apoptosis inhibition) and HMGB1 (cell proliferation and survival) indicates active suppression of differentiation-associated cell death during this biosynthetically intensive stage.
key_evidence: RPLP0, RPS17, RPS23: diagnostic ribosomal structural proteins indicating high translation demand
SNRPG, SNRPD1, SNRPE: snRNP core components essential for pre-mRNA splicing at scale during rapid biosynthesis
UQCRH, UQCRQ, NDUFS5: Complex III and Complex I subunits reflecting mitochondrial OXPHOS upregulation to fuel biosynthetic ATP demands
PTMA: antagonizes apoptosis during proliferative phase before terminal differentiation
PA2G4: ribosome biogenesis regulator, not ribosomal protein itself but facilitates assembly
suggested_validation: Co-stain sorted basophilic/pro-erythroblasts with FACS for Ki-67 (proliferation) and MitoTracker (mitochondrial mass) and correlate to SAE feature 1340 activation score; validate snRNP and OXPHOS expression by immunofluorescence on sorted populations at each erythroid stage

programme_name: Mitochondrial oxidative metabolism in proliferating precursors
functional_description: This feature marks metabolically active progenitor cells with elevated oxidative phosphorylation capacity and cytoskeletal dynamics. The co-enrichment of megakaryocyte precursors (39%) with activated dendritic cells and proliferating T cells suggests a proliferation-coupled metabolic state reliant on mitochondrial ATP synthesis and protein turnover. The elevated expression of COX5A, VDAC1, and SLC25A5 indicates robust mitochondrial bioenergetics supporting rapid cell division and differentiation capacity.
key_evidence: COX5A: Terminal respiratory chain enzyme diagnostic of high oxidative phosphorylation flux
VDAC1: Outer mitochondrial membrane porin required for ATP/ADP exchange in metabolically active cells
SLC25A5: Mitochondrial ADP/ATP carrier essential for coupling oxidative phosphorylation to biosynthesis
GSTP1: Elevated antioxidant defence counteracting ROS from active mitochondrial respiration
TMSB4X & COTL1: Actin cytoskeletal regulators supporting cell motility in precursor expansion
ENO1 & LDHA: Glycolytic enzymes enabling Crabtree effect in high-demand proliferation
suggested_validation: Quantify oxygen consumption rate (OCR) and extracellular acidification rate (EGCAR) in FACS-sorted megakaryocyte precursors vs. other haematopoietic progenitors, stratified by GSTP1/VDAC1 co-expression levels, to confirm mitochondrial oxidative dominance in this FP.

programme_name: Pro-B cell proliferation with open chromatin
functional_description: This feature captures actively cycling pro-B cells in S/G2M phase characterized by chromatin remodeling and transcriptional permissiveness. The dominant signature combines non-histone chromosomal proteins (HMGN1/2, HMGB1/2) that facilitate transcriptionally active chromatin architecture with microtubule dynamics (STMN1, TUBB) and protein synthesis machinery (RPS24, RPLP0, PPIA) required for rapid proliferation. PTMA provides anti-apoptotic function during intense metabolic activity of VDJ recombination-engaged lymphoid progenitors.
key_evidence: HMGN2/HMGN1: Non-histone nucleosomal proteins diagnostic of transcriptionally active, open chromatin in cycling cells
HMGB1/HMGB2: High mobility group proteins facilitating DNA access and chromatin remodeling during active transcription
STMN1: Microtubule destabilizer essential for mitotic spindle dynamics in proliferating cells; marker of S/G2M phase
PTMA: Nucleolar protein supporting ribosome biogenesis and anti-apoptosis during metabolically demanding VDJ recombination
TUBB, RPS24, RPLP0: Cytoskeletal and ribosomal protein synthesis components required for cell division
suggested_validation: Co-stain top-activating cells with Ki-67 (proliferation), phospho-histone H3 (mitotic phase), and ATAC-seq to confirm open chromatin accessibility coincides with HMGN/HMGB upregulation in pro-B cells undergoing VDJ recombination

programme_name: Early erythroid iron metabolism and ribosome biogenesis
functional_description: This programme represents early-stage erythroid progenitors (Pro-Erythroblasts and Basophilic Erythroblasts, 74% of cells) engaged in rapid proliferation with simultaneous activation of iron handling and ribosomal RNA processing. The coordinated upregulation of FTH1 (iron storage), BOLA3 (Fe-S cluster synthesis), and multiple ribosomal assembly factors (NOP10, PA2G4, METAP2) reflects the metabolic demands of haem synthesis and massive translational capacity needed for globin chain production during early erythroid expansion.
key_evidence: FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain—diagnostic iron storage activation essential for haem synthesis in early erythroid progenitors
BOLA3: Iron-sulfur cluster biosynthesis protein—required for cytochrome oxidase and other Fe-S-dependent respiratory enzymes needed to fuel erythroid proliferation
NOP10, PA2G4: H/ACA snoRNP components—activate ribosomal RNA modification and ribosome assembly, critical for translating massive quantities of globin mRNA
ATP5IF1, ATP5MC1, NME4: Mitochondrial ATP synthesis and energy metabolism—support the bioenergetic demands of early erythroid proliferation and haem synthesis
suggested_validation: Sort Pro-Erythroblasts and Basophilic Erythroblasts by FTH1/BOLA3 co-expression and perform oxygen consumption assays and Fe-S cluster quantification to confirm mitochondrial metabolic activation during early erythroid expansion

programme_name: Early erythroid-megakaryocyte proliferation checkpoint
functional_description: This programme marks the early bifurcation point between erythroid and megakaryocyte lineages, characterized by active nucleolar RNA processing (SRSF2/SRSF3 splicing), rapid protein synthesis (RPS24), and DNA damage checkpoint control (HMGB1, DEK). The dominance of pro-erythroblasts and megakaryocyte precursors with strong SR-protein and ribosomal gene expression indicates cells actively transitioning through G1/S phase with heightened transcriptional and translational demands before lineage commitment.
key_evidence: HMGB1: Nucleosomal packaging protein diagnostic of high transcriptional/replication activity during early progenitor proliferation
SRSF2/SRSF3: SR-family splicing factors essential for ribosomal and histone pre-mRNA processing during S-phase entry; markers of proliferative cells
RPS24: Ribosomal protein indicating intense protein synthesis supporting rapid cell division in cycling progenitors
DEK: Chromatin architecture protein involved in DNA damage response and mitotic checkpoint control; elevated in proliferating progenitors
RANBP1: Ran GTPase binding partner regulating nucleocytoplasmic transport; required for nuclear import of mitotic/replication machinery
PTMA: Prothymosin-α inhibits apoptosis and supports proliferation; marks cycling hematopoietic progenitors
suggested_validation: Co-stain top-200 cells with Ki-67 (proliferation) + CD34/CD41 (megakaryocyte) + CD71/GPA (erythroid) by flow cytometry to confirm this represents the G1/S-phase cycling progenitor compartment before lineage terminal differentiation.

programme_name: Megakaryocyte precursor proliferation and RNA processing
functional_description: This feature marks actively proliferating megakaryocyte precursors characterized by elevated nucleotide metabolism (GAPDH, ENO1), enhanced mitochondrial bioenergetics (VDAC1, SLC25A5), and coordinated upregulation of RNA splicing machinery (SRSF3, SNRPG, HNRNPC). The co-expression of DNA-binding proteins (HMGB1, HMGN2, YBX1) with splicing factors reflects the transcriptional and post-transcriptional remodeling required for rapid megakaryocytic differentiation and ploidy cycling.
key_evidence: SRSF3, SNRPG, HNRNPC: SR-rich splicing factors and hnRNPs diagnostic of active pre-mRNA processing during cell cycle progression
GAPDH, ENO1: Glycolytic enzymes indicating metabolic shift to support rapid biosynthesis in proliferating precursors
VDAC1, SLC25A5: Mitochondrial transporters reflecting enhanced oxidative phosphorylation and ATP demand during megakaryocyte maturation
HMGB1, HMGN2, YBX1: Chromatin-associated DNA-binding proteins facilitating open chromatin during proliferative phase
Cell composition: 79% megakaryocyte precursor enrichment validates lineage specificity despite 13% T proliferating contamination
suggested_validation: Co-stain CD34+ megakaryocyte precursors (CD41+/CD42b-) for Ki-67 and assess correlation with SRSF3/SNRPG protein expression by flow cytometry to confirm proliferation-linked splicing factor upregulation

programme_name: Megakaryocyte-erythroid progenitor S/G2M proliferation
functional_description: This programme captures actively proliferating megakaryocyte and erythroid progenitors in S/G2M phases, characterized by coordinated upregulation of histone mRNA-binding proteins (SLBP), ribosomal components (RPLP0, MRPS34), and RNA processing machinery (snRNPs, hnRNPs). The dominance of HMGB1, YBX1, and 14-3-3 proteins (YWHAQ/E) reflects chromatin remodelling and cell cycle checkpoint regulation required for massive DNA synthesis and protein production during megakaryocytic and erythroid amplification.
key_evidence: SLBP: diagnostic histone mRNA-binding protein specifically required for replication-dependent histone synthesis during S phase
RPLP0 + MRPS34: ribosomal proteins indicating active translation machinery for rapid protein synthesis in proliferating precursors
HMGB1 + YBX1: chromatin architectural and nucleic acid binding proteins required for chromatin accessibility during DNA replication
YWHAQ/YWHAE: 14-3-3 signalling mediators regulating G1/S and G2/M checkpoint progression in proliferating cells
NOP10 + snRNPs (SNRPE/SNRPG): snoRNP components involved in ribosomal RNA processing, essential for ribosome biogenesis during proliferation
suggested_validation: Cell cycle phase stratification (BrdU/EdU pulse labelling or Hoechst/PI analysis) of top-activating megakaryocyte precursors and basophilic erythroblasts to confirm predominance in S/G2M phases relative to other erythroid differentiation stages

programme_name: Megakaryocyte-erythroid progenitor proliferation and RNA processing
functional_description: This feature marks actively proliferating megakaryocyte precursors (51%) and early erythroblasts co-activating a coordinated programme of cell-cycle progression, mRNA splicing, and oxidative metabolism. The dominant upregulation of RNA processing factors (SRSF3, HNRNPA2B1, SNRPG, LSM5), protein quality control (YBX1, UBB, RBX1), and mitochondrial function (IDH2, NDUFB6, SOD1) indicates active protein synthesis demand during megakaryocyte and erythroid differentiation, particularly in the megakaryocyte precursor compartment.
key_evidence: YBX1: RNA-binding protein with nucleic acid binding and mRNA stability functions—diagnostic for high biosynthetic demand during proliferation
SRSF3, HNRNPA2B1, SNRPG, LSM5: SR-rich and spliceosomal proteins—indicate active pre-mRNA splicing required for cell-cycle genes and differentiation-specific transcripts
IDH2, NDUFB6, SOD1: TCA cycle and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation enzymes—reflect metabolic support for ATP-intensive megakaryopoiesis and erythropoiesis
RBX1, UBB, DEK: Ubiquitin-proteasome and E3-ligase components—support protein turnover during active differentiation and cell-cycle transit
YWHAQ, HMGB1: Signal transduction and chromatin remodelling proteins—facilitate cell-cycle checkpoints and transcriptional transitions in progenitors
suggested_validation: Co-immunofluorescence for CD34+CD41+ megakaryocyte precursors with Ki-67 and phospho-histone H3 to validate proliferation status; sort top-activating cells and perform RNA-seq to confirm elevated spliceosomal and mitochondrial gene expression relative to non-proliferating mature megakaryocytes and erythroblasts.

programme_name: Proliferative erythro-megakaryocyte progenitor ribosogenesis
functional_description: This programme marks early-stage erythroid and megakaryocytic progenitors (basophilic/polychromatic erythroblasts and megakaryocyte precursors) undergoing active proliferation. The signature is dominated by ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS17, RPL37A, RPS2, RPL7A, RPLP0) and translation machinery components (YBX1, RANBP1), indicating intense protein synthesis capacity during rapid cell division. Co-expression of RNA processing factors (SNRPG, SRSF3, SLBP) and the histone mRNA-binding protein SLBP specifically reflects the heightened histone demand during S-phase of proliferating erythroblasts and megakaryocyte precursors.
key_evidence: RPS24/RPS17/RPL37A/RPS2/RPL7A: Ribosomal protein cluster diagnostic of active translation in proliferating cells
YBX1/RANBP1: Nuclear-cytoplasmic protein trafficking and translation initiation factors essential for rapid protein synthesis
SLBP: Histone mRNA-binding protein specifically upregulated during S-phase; definitive marker of replication-dependent histone synthesis in proliferating erythroblasts
SRSF3/SNRPG: Pre-mRNA splicing factors required for processing of genes needed in active cell cycle progression
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of CD71+/CD34+ progenitors with BrdU/EdU incorporation and quantitative assessment of ribosomal protein translation (polysome profiling or selective ribosomal protein knockout effects on proliferation rates)

programme_name: Early erythroid proliferation stress response
functional_description: This programme captures metabolically active early erythroid progenitors (Pro-Erythroblasts and CFU-E) managing proliferative stress through coordinated activation of protein synthesis machinery (RPL37A, RPS23, DDX21), oxidative stress defences (TXN, SOD1), and nuclear/cytoplasmic proteostasis (LMNA, DNAJA1, HMGB1). The enrichment reflects the high biosynthetic demand of rapid cell division coupled with mitochondrial activity required for haem synthesis.
key_evidence: LMNA: Nuclear lamina integrity essential for cell cycle progression in rapidly dividing progenitors
TXN and SOD1: Redox buffering critical for managing ROS from intense mitochondrial haem synthesis
RPL37A, RPS23, DDX21: Ribosomal protein and RNA helicase support rapid translation demanded by proliferation
DNAJA1: HSP70 cochaperone managing proteostasis burden of biosynthetically active cells
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic function protects proliferating progenitors from stress-induced death
HMGB1: Nuclear stress sensor and chromatin regulator coordinately expressed in proliferative phase
suggested_validation: Quantify mtDNA content and real-time oxygen consumption in sorted Pro-Erythroblasts vs CFU-E to confirm mitochondrial activation; validate DNAJA1/TXN co-expression by immunofluorescence in these stages
